# The Arroyos

“

My life started when I met the Arroyos. Anything before that doesn't really matter to me.

— Ivy

The Arroyos are  Ivy's surrogate family that live in Spanish Harlem.

## Contents

- 1 Summary

- 1.1 Carlos Arroyo
- 1.2 Maria Arroyo
- 1.3 Sophia Arroyo
- 1.4 Manny Arroyo
- 2 Trivia
- 3 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

20 years before the ritual takes place,[1] the Arroyos were a small family that lived in Spanish Harlem while it was under Mendoza's control. One day, Sophia Arroyo and one of her parents were attacked in the streets by thugs, but were saved by  Ivy, who was then adopted by the Arroyos. For the next 18 years, Ivy spent her life fighting against the Mendoza Syndicate to free Spanish Harlem for the Arroyos.[2]

In the current day, the Arroyos live happily with Ivy in a Mendoza-free Spanish Harlem. Carlos and Maria had a son named "Manny", while Sophia was heading off for college. Ivy thinks the Arroyos are the best family in the world.[3]

Ivy is reluctant to leave the Arroyos on their own for too long.[4][5] This could be due to the fear that the Arroyos will be hurt if she's away from them.[6][7][8]

The Arroyos eat Mofongo, a traditional Puerto-Rican dish.[2][9]

The Arroyos are likely Catholic, based on Ivy's reaction to killing  Venator.[10][11]

There are four known Arroyos: Carlos, Maria, Sophia and Manny.

### Carlos Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Carlos Arroyo is the father of the family.

Carlos works as a first-grade teacher[12] and a community organiser for Spanish Harlem, however he's also running for mayor of New York.[13] In one pathway in Ivy's visual novel, Ivy supports Carlos' political campaign and participates in the ritual to help him become mayor.[14]

Infernus is voting for Carlos to become mayor.[15] Billy thinks Carlos is a fraud who uses Ivy for publicity and to increase the property value of Spanish Harlem.[16][17]

Carlos is worried about Ivy participating in the ritual.[18] He dislikes Fairfax Industries[19] and isn't thrilled about Ivy fighting against the OSIC during the ritual.[20]

Ivy idolises Carlos.[21][22] Carlos tells Ivy that it takes more muscles to frown than to smile.[23] He also says that "you can make opportunities, but you can't make people take them".[24]

### Maria Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Maria Arroyo is the mother of the family.

Not much is known about Maria, however she does have a date planned with Carlos at the Baroness Hotel.[25] Ivy also doesn't want her to know about Venator's involvement in the ritual.[11]

### Sophia Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Sophia Arroyo, also known as Sophie, is the elder daughter of the Arroyos. Based on her being a child when Ivy was brought to life, Sophia's age is likely in her mid-twenties.

Unknown to Ivy and the other Arroyos, Sophia works at  Wraith's casino, helping Wraith as her bookmaker.[26][27] In one pathway in Ivy's visual novel, Ivy discovers Sophia's secret job.[28] While the ending of that pathway is unknown, it likely results in Ivy participating in the ritual to keep Sophia safe.[29]

Sophia attends Columbia College as one of  Dynamo's students.[30] Sophia speaks highly of Dynamo[31][32] and Dynamo thinks she's a great student, but he is worried about her due to Sophia sleeping during lessons due to working long shifts at her job.[33] Dynamo is unaware that Sophia works for Wraith.

Sophia tells Ivy that, if she gets mad, she should hold her breath and count to four.[34]

Sophia was the Arroyo who named Ivy.[2]

Sophia listens to  Cadence's band.[35]

### Manny Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Manny Arroyo is the younger son of the Arroyos. Manny's age is unknown, however he's implied to still be in school.[36]

Manny seems to be a bookworm, as he loves reading about  Kelvin's adventures[37] and gets taken to libraries by Ivy for  Paige's Story Time.[38]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Spanish Harlem, also known as East Harlem or *El Barrio*, is a real New York neighborhood with majority Hispanic population.
- The Arroyos seem to be spelt "The Arroyo's" instead of "The Arroyos", based on Ivy's background.[2]
- The Doorman says that one of the Arroyos will die in 5 years, no matter what Ivy does.[7] This could be a bluff, but it's unknown.

# The Baxter Society

“

The Baxter Society has your number.

— Shiv

**The Baxter Society** is a well-known international monster hunting organization.

## Contents

- 1 Summary
- 2 Members
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Removed Lore
- 5 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Baxter Society was formed sometime after the First Maelstrom, with  Grey Talon as one of the founding members. The society has been operating for over 40 years, hunting monsters across the globe.[1] Currently, Shiv is the only named active Baxter Society member, with Grey Talon and  Calico being former members.

Instead of hunting all magical creatures, the Baxter Society specifically hunts monsters that prey on humanity.[1] This can extend to hunting humans, as Grey Talon mentions that the society likely would have hunted Lady Geist if they knew about her deal with Oathkeeper.[2] It's also mentioned that, while they currently aren't hunting them, the Baxter Society would likely hunt down, Seven.[3] The Baxter Society have been hunting Drifter for years, but have been unsuccessful at killing him.[4][5][6]

The members of the Baxter Society don't get paid to hunt monsters. The lack of payment was why Calico left the society to pursue the well-paid life of an assassin.[7] It's implied that Calico left the society before Shiv joined.[8]

Grey Talon, while retired, is still heavily respected by the Baxter Society.[9] His dedication to the society resulted in books being made about his life and earning him a reputation as a "legend".[10][11] His dedication to his work, however, meant he was often away from home, which meant he missed watching his son grow up.[12] Refusing to make the same mistake for his grandkids, Grey Talon retired after roughly 40 years of service.[13] When he retired, Grey Talon was said to have more confirmed kills than anyone else in the Baxter Society.[14]

Shiv was chosen by Grey Talon as his replacement.[15][16] Due to his criminal background, the other members of the Baxter Society don't trust or respect Shiv.[17][18] Shiv worries that the Baxter Society would eventually turn on him.[19] Shiv has been sent to the ritual on behalf of the Baxter Society,[20][21] and hopes that he can prove his worth to them and Grey Talon by hunting the Patrons.[22][23]

Holliday is disappointed that the Baxter Society isn't hunting the Troubadour. Shiv says the Society is dealing with their own problems, which could potentially be more dangerous than the Troubadour.[24] He also invites Holliday to join the Society if she manages to kill the Troubadour.[25]

The Baxter Society owns a manor house, which seems to be their main base of operations. Once, a member of the Paradox Organisation tried to break into the manor house, but was caught. Paradox wants Grey Talon to get her into the manor house.[26]

At some point, the Society had to intervene at the Baroness Hotel, which  The Doorman was grateful for.[27]

The Baxter Society have a friendly rivalry with the Venators of St. Benedict.[28]

According to Grey Talon, members of the society who are killed in action are often found skinless in a retention pond in Portugal or Denmark.[29]

Billy believes the Baxter Society never hunted any real monsters.[30]

### Chapter 1

[edit | edit source]

**1 - The Oathkeeper Problem**

*Lady Geist discovers that the ward keeping a malevolent spirit known as Oathkeeper bound to her is weakening.*

Johann visits Geist at her apartment. Geist hides the blood of her most recent victim under the rug. She complains that Oathkeeper is growing more restless and hungry. Johann analyses her ward and concludes that it is weakening. Johann and Geist look for ways to build a new ward, or an alternative to control Oathkeeper.

### Chapter 2

[edit | edit source]

**2a - Party Planning**

*Geist meets with Professor Dynamo to host a symposium on wards.*

**2b - Understanding Oathkeeper**

*Geist meets with Johann to discuss Oathkeeper.*

[edit | edit source]

**3a - The Gala**

*Geist has an encounter with someone who can help her.*

**3b - Hunger Strike**

*Geist threatens Oathkeeper in order to get him to agree to finding a new host.*

*Geist dreams of the day she made her original deal with Oathkeeper.*

[edit | edit source]

*Geist meets with Detective Abrams.*

*Geist reveals to Johann the lengths she will go to in order to ensure her survival.*

*Geist tries to work off 50 years of life that she hadn't paid Oathkeeper for.*

*Geist tries to make Maximilian Fairfax an irresistible offer.*

**5g - The Sacrifice**

*Geist decides Johann's fate. (Endings: Sacrifice Him; Be Selfless)*

**5i - All Good Things**

*Geist makes peace with Oathkeeper and herself.*

## Chapter 1: The Oathkeeper Problem

[edit | edit source]

*Doorbell rings. Dr. Johann Jr. enters Lady Geist's apartment.*

**Lady Geist:** Apologies for the mess, I had company over last night.

**Johann Jr.:** I can see that...

**Lady Geist:** If it makes you uncomfortable you can wait outside while I...

**Johann Jr.:** No, no, i-it's fine...

**Lady Geist:** You're very convincing, doctor...

**Johann Jr.:** I'm sorry, it's just that seeing it is different than...

**Lady Geist:** Of course, of course... Let me, ah, move the rug.

*Lady Geist covers a blood stain on the floor with a rug.*

**Johann Jr.:** Thank you. So!.. What's going on?

**Lady Geist:** It's Oathkeeper. He's... Stronger? Angrier? Hungrier? I don't know. Life doesn't sustain me the way that it used to. Oh, don't look at me like that! You're safe here.

**Johann Jr.:** Tell that to the last guy...

**Lady Geist:** If I wanted to talk to the last guy I probably wouldn't have killed him.

**Johann Jr.:** You're hilarious. Let me see your arm.

*Johann Jr. inspects Oathkeeper's lock.*

**Lady Geist:** Your dad would have laughed at my jokes.

**Johann Jr.:** My dad had a horrible sense of humor.

**Lady Geist:** He was a good man.

**Johann Jr.:** He did his best.

*Johann Jr. finishes his inspection.*

**Johann Jr.:** The lock is still intact, but... the ward is getting weaker.

**Lady Geist:** You reapplied the ward 5 years ago!

**Johann Jr.:** I know. It's concerning.

**Lady Geist:** How concerning?..

**Johann Jr.:** How long have you had Oathkeeper trapped in your arm? Thirty years?

**Lady Geist:** Closer to f... 50.

**Johann Jr.:** Very concerning! Do you know how the warding actually works?

**Lady Geist:**  Just the basics. Your father described it as a puzzle box that Oathkeeper would be compelled to open... and that the more focus and energy he exerts unraveling the ward the less he has to make demands of me.

**Johann Jr.:** Well, after 50 years, it looks like Oathkeeper got better at multitasking.

**Lady Geist:**  So build a better ward!

**Johann Jr.:** I can't.

**Lady Geist:** A pity. I don't maintain relationships with... useless people.

**Johann Jr.:** I thought I was safe here!

**Lady Geist:** And I thought you were good at your job! We both made mistakes.

**Johann Jr.:** I can't tell if you're joking.

**Lady Geist:** Do you want to find out? Or would you rather just propose a solution?

**Johann Jr.:** There might be some... alternatives.

**Lady Geist:** And I can't *wait* to hear them.

**Choice between:**

*Try To Understand Wards Better* - *Try To Understand Oathkeeper Better*

[edit | edit source]

## 2a - Party Planning

[edit | edit source]

Follows from Chapter 1 if "Try To Understand Wards Better" was picked.

*Lady Geist visits Dynamo during one of his lectures at Columbia University.*

**Dynamo:** ... And that concludes today's lecture on ley lines... Don't forget to review your notes on Astral Gates tonight, there will be a pop quiz tomorrow. Please act surprised.

**Lady Geist:** Hello, professor. I believe Johann told you to expect me.

**Dynamo:** Uh, he said his grandmother would like to have a chat, but you don't...

**Lady Geist:** I moisturize.

**Dynamo:** Ah, yes... You're the one with the, uh... "Condition".

**Lady Geist:** Indeed.

**Dynamo:** The intersection between magic, medicine and science is a fascinating one, isn't it?

**Lady Geist:** Riveting.

**Dynamo:** It's so exciting to find a kindred spirit! Have you been going to Brown's recent lecture series? If not, you absolutely must-

**Lady Geist:** My time is at a premium, professor. The longer we chit-chat, the more likely your course is the only one at Columbia with a body count.

**Dynamo:** Alright, then... How can I help?

**Lady Geist:** My ward is failing.

**Dynamo:** A dire situation, to be sure... but I'm afraid my knowledge of binding wards is journeyman at best.

**Lady Geist:** Yes, but your connections with science and academia are vast.

**Dynamo:** "Vast", that's, uh... That's very generous of you.

**Lady Geist:** I want to host a bit of a... symposium on my... condition, as you called it. More of a gala, really. It's pivotal that the right people are in attendance. The brightest minds.

**Dynamo:** Oh, I imagine I can drum up some interest. Uh, when next year are you thinking?

**Lady Geist:** Oh, it's in two weeks.

**Dynamo:** Ah-uh-that's simply impossible. The sort of folks you want to speak with are taking sabbaticals, or doing field research... And as we both know, no one's leaving the Black Chateau to come to your event.

**Lady Geist:** For every expert you bring, I will donate a quarter-million dollars to your department.

**Dynamo:** Annnd what a gala it will be! I'll get you a list of names soon.

**Lady Geist:** Thank you, professor.

**Followed by:**

*"The Gala"*

**Johann Jr.:** I don't, and that's why you have a chance... Oma, you are a uniquely cruel woman, and Oathkeeper has to respect that on some level. That thing *lives* to make deals, so make it another one.

**Lady Geist:** I have no leverage, why would he... oh my god. Of course... he doesn't know how close he is to breaking free, does he?

**Johann Jr.:** I don't think so.

**Fairfax:** So. What can we do for each other?

**Fairfax:** I have enemies. "Powerful" is a bit generous. [Scoffs], says the crone who's conviced the world she's in the prime of her life.

**Lady Geist:** I see you've heard the rumors. Good. That saves me time. Your confidence is inspiring; unfortunately, reality does not bend around your bravado...

**Fairfax:** So Oathkeeper...

**Lady Geist:** Is very real.

**Fairfax:** Ahh, and you...

**Lady Geist:** I'm tired of bearing his weight.

**Fairfax:** Go on.

**Lady Geist:** Something this powerful can't be left to its own devices. It needs guidance. A strong hand... Something you alone can provide.

**Fairfax:** Yes, yes, and in exchange?

**Lady Geist:** There are some... guarantees that I'd like to see in place in regards to my foundations as well as my safety.

**Fairfax:** I assume you'll want a blood contract?

**Lady Geist:** Naturally.

**Fairfax:** I can have a notary here in a few days. Should be plenty of time to settle on terms.

**Lady Geist:** Wonderful.

*Cuts to 3 days later. The blood contract has been signed and Oathkeeper is now bound to Fairfax.*

**Lady Geist:** I'm glad we were able to come to an agreement.

**Fairfax:** Oathkeeper is in safe hands.

**Lady Geist:** Maximilian, so long as I'm in safe hands, I'm satisfied.

*Lady Geist leaves.*

**Fairfax:** So. Oathkeeper... Are you ready to change the world?

**Oathkeeper:** Mr. Fairfax, I thought you'd never ask.

[edit | edit source]

# The Curiosity Shop

Shop logo

“

You want hexes? We got hexes! You need bullets? We got bullets! You need a Reuben? Find a deli, because in the Curiosity Shop, we deal in power and tchotchkes!

— The Shopkeeper

**The Curiosity Shop** is the place players go to purchase various items from the Shopkeeper.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Functions

- 2.1 Buying
- 2.2 Selling
- 2.3 Imbuing
- 2.4 Active Items
- 2.5 Shop Bonus
- 3 Shop Locations

- 3.1 Base Shop
- 3.2 Side Shop
- 3.3 Secret Shop
- 4 Lore
- 5 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Curiosity Shop in-game.

The Curiosity Shop is the main form of progression in matches of *Deadlock*, giving players access to dozens of powerful items available for the player to purchase using  **** Souls. These items provide a variety of different stat increases and bonuses for the player, modifying things like ammo, fire rate, damage of abilities and weapons, ability range and cooldowns, movement speed, etc, along with passive buffs and additional active abilities.

Items are split into three categories; the two damage types, Weapon and Spirit, and Vitality for defense.

These shops are scattered throughout the map with one at each base, towards mid on both teams sides, along with every lane's first Guardians, although these close after the Guardian is killed. They can be found by heading towards the shop icon on the minimap (). Players can interact with shops by standing in front of them within the small yellow rectangle and pressing their open shop keybind.

Every hero also has a set of items in their Default build separated into sections for the early, mid, and late game as determined by the developers. Players are also capable of creating and sharing their own builds for each hero.

Some items are components, which can be upgraded into more expensive items with improved effects.

## Functions

[edit | edit source]

Shop UI

### Buying

[edit | edit source]

Items can be purchased using Souls and are separated into 4 different tiers based on their price: 800, 1,600, 3,200 and 6,400. Items with components can be bought in their entirety or get upgraded into from their components for their price minus the Souls already spent on the components.

### Selling

[edit | edit source]

Items can be sold back to the shop for half of the initial amount of Souls spent on them, or entirely refunded if the player has not left the shop area after first purchasing an item, freeing up item slots for the player. Any Unsecured Souls spent on the item will be refunded as Secured, if the player gets the full refund.

### Imbuing

[edit | edit source]

When certain items are purchased, the player is prompted to imbue one of their hero's abilities, giving them an additional bonus in the stat that item is improving. For example, when buying  Surge of Power, one ability can be chosen to have extra Spirit Power, allowing for further ability specialization.

### Active Items

[edit | edit source]

When buying an Active Item, players are prompted to place it into one of 4 ability slots in addition to their normal item slots. Players can only have a maximum of 4 Active Items in their inventory at a time, even if they have open item slots available to purchase more. Once a player has 4 Active Items, no more Active Items can be purchased until an Active Item is sold.

### Shop Bonus

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Item Types

When buying items, the player gains bonus stats related to the item's category: Weapon Damage for Weapon, Health for Vitality, and Spirit Power for Spirit.

## Shop Locations

[edit | edit source]

Showcase shop locations for the Hidden King's team.
Base Shops in green
Side Shops in blue
Secret Shops in yellow
Enemy shops are colored red

### Base Shop

[edit | edit source]

The base shop can be found at spawn. Unlike other shops, the buying radius extends to the whole area of the spawn room. Players can only buy items at their own base's shop.

### Side Shop

[edit | edit source]

By every lane there is a side shop available, allowing quick purchases without leaving the lane. However, if the lane's Guardian is destroyed, the side shop closes and will not sell any items for the rest of the match. Players can only buy items at their own team's side shops; with the exception of  Rem,  who can send his  Lil Helpers to purchase queued items from any shop on the map (with the exception of either team's Base Shop).

### Secret Shop

[edit | edit source]

Both sides have their own secret shop, which can be found in an underground tunnel accessible by stairs or an open manhole. They are located midway between Broadway Street and the outside lanes. From the player's perspective, the secret shop on the right side of the map (Green for Hidden King and Yellow for Archmother) is in their teams' side. Both teams can access and make purchases from either secret shop.

## Lore

[edit | edit source]

The Curiosity Shop's item catalogs are provided by Fairfax Industries, Mystic Pharmaceutical Stores, and the Curiosity Catalog.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The side shops had wheels and tracks leading to each team's base, indicating that at one point in development they were supposed to move along the lanes. This was changed after the Map Rework update.
- Before the October 2nd 2025 update, Secret Shops temporarily closed when players from both teams were nearby.[1]
- The shape of shop's minimap icon is more reminiscient of its appearance in Neon Prime

# The Cursed Apple

“

Welcome to New York! Need a gun?

— The Shopkeeper

**The Cursed Apple** or **"The Map"** is the default location where matches take place in *Deadlock*. It is a small segment of the game's version of Midtown and Lower Manhattan in New York City, in which the Heroes fight to complete The Ritual and summon their respective Patron. Players can navigate with a Minimap.

The current map is called *dl_midtown*. Previous versions of the map were called *street_test* and *dl_streets*.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Layout
- 1.2 Juke Rooms
- 1.3 Objectives
- 1.4 Player Visibility
- 2 Map Icons
- 3 Map Timings and Events

- 3.1 2:00
- 3.2 5:00
- 3.3 6:00
- 3.4 8:00
- 3.5 10:00
- 3.6 30:00
- 4 Territory
- 5 Trivia
- 6 Gallery
- 7 See also
- 8 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

A Juke Room, with a shadow figure in its doorway.

### Layout

[edit | edit source]

The map is divided into three distinct lanes: **York** (Yellow Lane), **Broadway** (Blue Lane) and **Park** (Green Lane), also referred to as **Greenwich**. Outside of these lanes are a series of tunnels, alleyways, and buildings that sometimes contain Golden Statues, crates, and neutral Denizens. In each lane, a Zipline extends from both bases directly overhead with each having the color of the corresponding lane. The Hidden King's side of the map has mostly worn down red brick buildings, while the Archmother's side has mostly upper class white brick buildings.

Throughout the map, players can find destructible Boxes and Golden Statues. Boxes have a 60% chance to drop souls upon being destroyed, and Golden Statues have a 50% chance to drop permanent stat bonuses, such as Spirit Power or Weapon Damage. They spawn 2 minutes into the game (except mid-boxes, see Map Timings and Events : 10min) and will respawn 3 minutes after being destroyed.

Outside of the lanes is an area of the map called the jungle, which is home to the neutral Denizen camps. Denizens are alien-like entities that appear in groups and will attack when provoked. They come in three different sizes: small, medium and large, and drop more souls the larger they are. Being neutral units, both teams can attack the same denizen camps, and they will be aggressive to their attackers no matter which team they are on.

### Juke Rooms

[edit | edit source]

Juke Rooms are small dead-end tunnels located in specific points around the map. They are marked prominently by their shadowy figure standing in their doorways that contains a cosmic veil. Above the doorways is a red rectangular sign, and in the compartment contains candles and a small wall light. Juke Rooms - as implied by their name - are most often used to hide or corner enemies, as they have only one entrance. The doorway shadow also acts as a warning for fleeing players that they are about to walk into a dead-end.

A player, upon pinging a lane, has their hero state which lane they are headed to.

### Objectives

[edit | edit source]

In each lane on either team's side, there are a series of powerful defensive structures that must be destroyed in order to reach the enemy base. The first is the Guardian, followed by the Walker and finally a pair of weaker Base Guardians. In each team's base are two Shrines, which must be destroyed in order to attack the main objective: the Patron. The Patron has two phases, and will shift to the second one after the first phase has been defeated. Destroying the now weakened Patron is the condition for winning a match.

In the very middle of the map, in the underground sewer, is a second major objective known as the Mid-Boss. It is a large alien creature similar to the Denizens, possessing a very large health pool, a constantly regenerating shield and a highly dangerous laser beam. After being slain, it will spawn a Rejuvenator Crystal that can be claimed by either team. The claimer's team will be bestowed with the Rejuvenation Credit buff, granting them special effects.

### Player Visibility

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Minimap

An important aspect of the map is spotting where enemies are located. An enemy player is visible to the team if they are either in a team player's line of sight, or shooting Troopers or Structures. A player can press Tab and middle-click the enemies' portrait to ping to their allies that said enemy is missing, which is useful if they have left their lane.

## Territory

[edit | edit source]

An important part of *Deadlock* is managing the clash of Troopers that occurs in each lane. Killing enemy Troopers allows allied Troopers to move further into the lane. This extends the Zipline available to the player's team on that lane. The Ziplines on the map will show how far a lane is "pushed" towards the enemy base, how far the Zipline can take the player, and if any lanes are in need of help with a quick glance.
Teleporters can be used to quickly traverse the map horizontally.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Before the Map Rework Update, the map had 4 lanes. The fourth was Purple (Park). Green Lane was initially called Greenwich, then replaced Park, and is now Greenwich again, though still labeled as Park in the Zipline UI.  The center of the map was the Museum, now reworked as the Archmother base.
- Green (Greenwich) originally supplanted Orange (Orchard).
- All the lanes are named after real New York streets. The team's bases used to be named after the train stations Grand Central (Archmother) and Penn Station (Hidden King).
- Towards the right of the team's bases is a Bull and a Bear Statue, respectively located at the Museum (Archmother) and the Factory (Hidden King). These statues are symbolic to the market conditions of a stock market. On a related note, the Bull Statue has a real world counterpart in New York.
- The Statue of Liberty can be seen behind the dock on Yellow Lane.
- The map used to be called *street_test*, and was later changed to *dl_streets* in one of the updates, until it was replaced by *dl_midtown*. *street_test* and *dl_streets* can still be accessed in-game with the console command map street_test and map dl_streets, although the former's lighting was broken by updates.
- There used to be a map in the files called *caldera_trooper,* which featured assets from both *Neon Prime* and early *Deadlock* builds. It has since been removed, but was archived by modders. A tour and comparison of *caldera_trooper* was made by YouTube channel DeadAir. Left side of the Sandbox map was based off it.
- Other unused maps currently accessible in the game files that use *Neon Prime* assets are called *start*, *1v1_test* and *hero_testing*.
- Many of the buildings in the Cursed Apple's skyline are based on real New York buildings from the early 1900s.[1]
- The Juke Room shadows are actually 3D models rendered with transparency. There are 4 models: A tall man wearing a fedora, a short man wearing a postman hat, a woman, and a child holding a box.

# The Deep

“

I was hoping that this suit would make people take the problems of the Deep seriously. I'm not sure it's working.

— Viscous

**The Deep** is an underwater location within the depths of the Bermuda Triangle. It is connected to Outer Planes via an Astral Gate.

## Contents

- 1 Summary

- 1.1 The Adversary
- 2 Trivia
- 3 Removed Lore
- 4 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

Described as a shadowline nexus deep below the Atlantic Ocean, the Deep is an underwater habitat where an Astral Gate resides.[1] As the Deep is deep underwater, the surface world doesn't interact with it much, making its culture significantly different from the surface.[2]

Viscous is a denizen of the Deep.[1] The Loch Ness Monster also came from the Deep's Astral Gate.[1]

The Deep is being threatened by a "genocidal force of nature" known as The Adversary, who came through the Deep's Astral Gate. The denizens of the Deep are terrified of the Adversary, as they are currently getting "massacred" by the monster.[3]

Viscous says the other denizens find legs "unnerving", but he enjoys having them.[4]

Calico has knowledge about the Deep.[5][6]

The OSIC seems to worry about the creatures of the Deep.[7]

### The Adversary

[edit | edit source]

The Adversary is a powerful and dangerous being who came through the Deep's Astral Gate. Currently, the Adversary is massacring the denizens of the Deep, and Viscous believes that, if he can't stop the Adversary, it's only a matter of time before the Adversary starts killing everything on the surface.[8][9]

Viscous has entered the ritual to stop the Adversary, hoping to get rid of it to save the Deep.[1]

Most playable characters are unaware of what's happening in the Deep, and don't take the threat of the Adversary seriously.[10] Billy refuses to believe in the Adversary unless he sees it with his own eyes.[11] It's implied that the surface often ignores the troubles of the Deep.[12][13]

Viscous asks Grey Talon if the Baxter Society could help stop the Adversary if he fails to summon the Patrons.[14]

Haze is aware of the Adversary and takes the situation seriously as she knows it's only a matter of time until the Adversary becomes a problem on the surface.[15] She asks Viscous to tell her everything about the Adversary so the OSIC can be prepared in case more creatures like it come through the Deep's Astral Gate.[16]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Holliday mistakes the Deep for the American Deep South. She asks Viscous if he's from Mobile, Alabama.[17]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

Unused hero  Fathom was also a denizen of the deep.[18] Before the Adversary came along, Fathom was the apex predator of the Deep.[18]

Some denizens of the Deep used to worship Fathom, begging him to save their lives from The Adversary.[19] The denizens of the Deep know Fathom's "true name".[20]

Fathom's motivation in the ritual was to stop the Adversary to regain his status as the apex predator.[18]

“

Hurting them is fine, but *vexing* them is even better.

**The Doorman** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He's proper, he's polite, but the humble Doorman of The Baroness Hotel is more than meets the eye. A brisk ring of his Call Bell leaves nearby enemies disoriented, and his high-speed Luggage Cart knocks them right off their feet. Do you find yourself getting lost easily in the streets of Manhattan? Don't worry, The Doorman is here to provide a shortcut with his Doorway whenever the need arises. And only the most special of enemies get to experience the trip of a lifetime to The Baroness Hotel.

A self-described "Fledgling God" and possibly a cosmic being of some repute, **the Doorman**  planned to experience life on this material plane of humanity for only a few weeks. After a few odd encounters and interactions, he quickly decided to remain as a simple doorman within the New York service industry to continue observing the strange demands that please humans.

The Doorman was released on August 22, 2025 as the third hero of the Six New Heroes update (second winner of hero vote).

NotesTipsShow All

- When returning from the Baroness, players receive a fading Time Slow for 1s.
- If the player falls off the platforms, they are sent back to the beginning of the map.
- Players can avoid the damage by becoming invincible, such as with  Ethereal Shift or  Dynamo's  Quantum Entanglement, or by blocking the damage with  Counterspell. This works both on a successful exit (if used before the fadeout) and a failed one. However, in the latter case, it will still trigger the T3 cooldown reduction.
- The player cannot activate abilities that would allow them to teleport back to the Cursed Apple from the Baroness or vice-versa, such as  Pocket's  Flying Cloak or  Mirage's  Traveler.  Sinclair also cannot cast  Spectral Assistant while inside the Baroness.
- Target is frozen in place and cannot act during channel time. The target's channels are cancelled upon entering the Baroness (except  Ivy's  Air Drop which is ended immediately, but will drop the bomb/ally if she holds one). Channeling abilities with cast delays can still activate if the delay started before Hotel Guest's channel and end before entering, such as  Yamato's  Power Slash.

- Applying movement slow to a target before casting Hotel Guest (e.g.  Call Bell,  Cold Front) makes it more likely the victim triggers extra damage and T2/T3 upgrades.
- The "turning keys" animation on target's body is a good indicator to time throwing a  Call Bell or launching  Luggage Cart into returning victim.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- A possible inspiration for the Doorman is the hero concept Frynd Leeman by player Onennon on the *Deadlock* forums. Like the Doorman, Frynd is a tall, gaunt, ancient, mysterious figure who works a service job (originally an innkeeper) to learn more about humans, and uses keys as his weapon. Abilities include opening door portals in the map, summoning a magic cart, and opening a portal to their domain.
- Every map in the game has a hidden copy of the Baroness Hotel room. The Doorman's ultimate cannot be used in maps that don't have the hotel room.
- The Doorman was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidentally leaked on stream in May 2025.
- The Doorman's Doorway ability summons one orange portal and one blue portal, similar to Valve's game *Portal*.
- According to developer Kaori, the Doorman's voice actor is a stage actor on his first video game role.[1]
- "At Your Service in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as The Doorman in the Hideout.
- The Doorman had the closest winning difference in the Six New Heroes contest, beating  Paige by only 0.85%.[2]
- The description for *Deadlock* in Steam Replay 2025 reads *"The Baroness is always looking for new guests"*, repeating the Doorman's voiceline[3].

“

It’s important to never overlook the help.

He's proper, he's polite, but the humble Doorman of The Baroness Hotel is more than meets the eye.

While he had only planned to experience life on this plane for a few weeks, The Doorman quickly discovered that the New York service industry was a great way to see the strange demands that please humans.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman's motivation in the ritual is to see the Patrons, since he hasn't seen them in a long time.[1][2] He doesn't seem to have a wish planned as he intends to return to the Baroness after the ritual,[3][4] although the Patrons goad him to wish back his old power.[5]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman is referred to as a fledgling god (by himself),[6] a Patron (by himself)[7] and a cosmic being.[8] He often refers to the other heroes as "mortals".[9][10]

"The Doorman" is not the Doorman's real name, but one he uses to "keep himself grounded" to remind himself that he's here to serve, not to rule.[11]

There are lines which imply that, a long time ago, Doorman used to slaughter humans, expressing glee at the chance to kill again and be feared during the ritual.[12][13] The true nature of the Doorman is unknown to most of the cast.[14]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman is polite and respectful when talking to the other heroes.

### Information

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman likes working at the Baroness since he gets to observe humanity.[15]

The OSIC seem to be aware of the Doorman's true nature, as they consider Doorman participating in the ritual as "overstepping".[16]

The Doorman claims to be able to see the future.[17]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### The Patrons

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman calls the Patrons "old friends" and refers to them as City Mother and Amber King.[18][19]

Both Patrons are familiar with the Doorman, expressing surprise and joy at seeing him fighting on their behalf.[20][21] They respect The Doorman and view his murderous side as "who he was meant to be".[22]

-Infernus

-Lady Geist(?)

-Wraith(?)

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- The Doorman is extremely knowledgeable about every other hero in the game, tormenting them while they're trapped in the Baroness.[23] He doesn't seem to know what  Warden wants,[24] which could mean he's telepathic like the Patrons as opposed to being omniscient, since they can't read Warden's desires either.[25]
- The Doorman respects  Infernus since they both work in the service industry and is apologetic when killing him.[26][27]
- The Doorman thinks  Wraith is a "delight" and is grateful towards her since she's a generous tipper.[28][29]
- The Doorman thinks  Lady Geist is rude and doesn't expect any tips from her.[30][31]
- The Doorman is actively keeping  Paradox out of the Baroness.[32]
- The Doorman has kicked  Silver and  Vyper out of the Baroness.[33][34]
- Both Patrons are familiar with the Doorman, expressing surprise and joy at seeing him fighting on their behalf.[20][21] They respect The Doorman and view his murderous side as "who he was meant to be".[22]
- Mina and  Lady Geist don't like talking to The Doorman since they view him as just "the help".[35][36]
- Venator recognises that Doorman is more ancient and powerful than he lets on.[37][38]
- Seven knows that Doorman isn't normal and wants to uncover his secrets.[39][40]

# The Hidden King

Overview

Quotes

The Hidden King

“

The stretching shadow of a skyscraper... a boarded-up apartment in Hell’s Kitchen... The Hidden King exists in the cracks of the city, waiting for his followers to usher him into the light.

— Old Gods, New Blood Update

**The Hidden King** is a Patron, as well as the name of his Team. His followers are **The Hidden King's Court**. The Archmother is his rival.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Gallery
- 3 Trivia
- 4 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Hidden King appears as a shadowy figure with antlers and glowing yellow eyes, bound to a burning wicker man effigy. Long, claw-like yellow hands extend from the shadows. His base is a factory filled with large speakers and microphones, and his side of the map features working-class red brick buildings labeled "Downtown".

The Hidden King does not speak to the heroes directly. Instead, a herald speaks on his behalf.[1][2][3]

Akin to the Archmother, the Hidden King's goals are unknown. According to The Doorman, the Hidden King has wanted to be summoned for "centuries".[4] Warden and his family believe the Patrons will "herald the end of humanity" if left unchecked.[5] It's implied that the Hidden King wants to "usher in his new era".[6][7]

The Hidden King's herald mentions that the Hidden King is "returning to us".[2]

The Doorman refers to the Hidden King as **Amber King**.[8]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Hidden King's name and appearance have similarities to The King in Yellow, a fictional supernatural entity created by Robert W. Chambers.
- The Hidden King was originally named **The Amber Hand** prior to the Old Gods, New Blood update. He also referred to himself as **Anvil's Song** in a removed voice line. This is referenced in a Warden unselect line.[9]

- A proposed rename to the Hidden King was **The Broken Crown**.
- The Hidden King announcer's voice actor was recast with the new model in the Old Gods, New Blood update. The current voice is speculated to be either Clancy Brown (Mr. Krabs in *Spongebob Squarepants*) or Darin De Paul (Reinhardt in *Overwatch*). Developer Kaori has so far chosen not to reveal the name of either the current or previous voice actor to not "spoil the fun".[10] They have also said that the previous Amber Hand actor can still be heard in the game in a different role.[11]

# The Library

“This is going to be exciting!”

This page contains game content that is unfinished, work in progress, or unavailable in standard gameplay.

The Library menu.

**The Library** is an upcoming *Deadlock* feature. The Library will contain visual novels that will expand the world and lore of *Deadlock* through interactive, branching narratives.

It is expected that cosmetic items may be unlocked as rewards for completing the visual novel paths.

The Library used to be accessible in-game in an earlier build, but has since been removed.

# The Mendoza Syndicate

“

I took out Mendoza, and I'll take out you!

— Ivy (to Yamato)

**The Mendoza Syndicate** was a crime syndicate located in Spanish Harlem, named after its leader **Mendoza**.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

Around 1929, the Mendoza Syndicate controlled Spanish Harlem. Members of the Syndicate harassed innocent people, including the Arroyo family. At this time, the gargoyle that would become known as  Ivy came to life and protected the Arroyos. Ivy was named and adopted by the family and vowed to dismantle the Mendoza Syndicate and free Spanish Harlem. She dedicated 18 years of her life to this mission.[1]

Ivy tells  Vindicta that she was able to take down the Syndicate "without murdering everybody."[2]

Yamato thanks Ivy for taking care of Mendoza.[3] However, she also undermines Ivy's skill and says she wants to take over Spanish Harlem for the Seventh Moon.[4][5]

Wraith admires Ivy for "making Mendoza's life hell." Ivy is wary of Wraith and warns her to stay away from Spanish Harlem.[2]

### Mendoza

[edit | edit source]

Mendoza is described as a "good client" by  Krill, and a "bad man" by Ivy.[2]

He told Wraith that  Lash would take a dive in a fight, which she lost money betting on. Lash says Mendoza "says a lot of stupid shit."[6]

The leaked audio for Ivy's visual novel implies that Mendoza promised to leave New York, but instead went into hiding. Ivy and Lash will be going after him.

# The New York Oracle

The New York Oracle billboard
The New York Oracle Newscaster

“

The New York Oracle, bringing the future to the present for over 20 years.

— The Newscaster

The **New York Oracle** is an in-universe newspaper publication in Deadlock that has been operating in New York for over 20 years, costing 5 pennies per copy.

In-game, it takes the form of a stall on the lanes with the Newscaster NPC. Although it can't be interacted with, it will periodically say one of the headlines, which give insights to nearby players about the world and setting of the game. The Newscaster model is similar to the Shopkeeper. The Newscaster also narrates the in-game tutorial.

Allie Kincaid is a reporter for the New York Oracle.

The Newscaster is voiced by Jason Keller, who also voices the Shopkeeper.[1]

## Contents

- 1 Locations
- 2 Headlines
- 3 Seasonal (Winter)

- 3.1 Hero Headlines
- 4 Trivia

[edit | edit source]

The Newscaster can be found in 2 locations across the Cursed Apple.

- Close to the Hidden King's base in the Yellow lane
- Close to the Archmother's base in the Green lane

# The Troubadour

“

When I find who I'm looking for, I'm not bringing him in. I'm putting him down.

— Holliday

**"The Troubadour"** is the name given by media for a serial killer who commited a killing spree in the town of Macomb in central Illinois.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Troubadour was confronted by the town's sheriff,  Holliday, but he managed to escape by turning into a murder of crows and flying away, although Holliday still has been looking for him. Both she and the New York Oracle speculate that The Troubadour is flying from Champaign–Urbana to New York.[1] Holliday's visual novel tells the story of her hunt for the Troubadour.

It is implied that Holliday's late sister might have been a victim of the Troubadour.[2][3]

The Drifter tells  Infernus that he's not the Troubadour, and that he only knows him by reputation.[4] He claims to be more dangerous than the Troubadour,[5] and advises Holliday against hunting the Troubadour.[6]

Holliday is disappointed that the Baxter Society isn't hunting the Troubadour.  Shiv says the Society is dealing with their own problems, which could potentially be more dangerous than the Troubadour.[7]  Calico says she knows enough about the Troubadour to stay away from him.[8]

One of Holliday's post-visual novel interaction with  Seven suggests that the OSIC wants to recruit the Troubadour.[9]

According to  The Doorman, the Troubadour's actions in Macomb took away the Baroness' title of "most haunted hotel in America".[10]

## References

[edit | edit source]

1. ↑ Newscaster's in-game voice line   - *"A murder of crows suspected to be the infamous serial killer known as 'The Troubadour' was spotted flying over Champaign-Urbana today. Could he be flying to New York?"*
1. ↑ Holliday And Ivy Conversation 1 -  *"My sister's dead."*
1. ↑ Holliday And Grey Talon Conversation 3 -  *"I know that look in your eyes. Who did they take from you? (...) I hope today we both find peace."*
1. ↑ Drifter And Infernus Conversation 2 -  *"Level with me. Are you the Troubadour?"* -  *"While I do have a song in my heart, I'm not. (...) Never met the man, just know him by reputation."*
1. ↑ Drifter's in-game  voice line  - *"The Troubadour ain’t got nothin’ on me."*
1. ↑ Drifter And Holliday Conversation 1 -  *"You don't wanna find him. (...)  Macomb matters a lot to you, but to him it was just a fun time that'll get lost in the ocean of memory. But if you find him, if he knows he got his hooks in you, you gonna be his hobby."*
1. ↑ Holliday And Shiv Conversation 2 -  *"We got our own problems right now. (...) Trust me Sheriff, if we don't clean up our own house you'll be wishing for Troubadour-sized problems."*
1. ↑ Holliday And Calico Conversation 2 -  *"You ever hear of something called 'The Troubadour'?"* -  *"Enough to know to stay away from it."*
1. ↑ Holliday And Seven Conversation 3 (post-visual novel) -  *"I can't believe the OSIC wanted to recruit that thing."*
1. ↑ The Doorman And Grey Talon Conversation 3 -  *"The Baroness still the most haunted hotel in America?"* -  *"Just the tri-state area, I’m afraid. That ghastly business in Macomb pulled a lot of mid-west specters."*

# The Tunnel Rats

“

You're going to wish you had the Tunnel Rats on your side.

— Krill

The Tunnel Rats are an underground (both figuratively and literally) group that assists the black market that operates between the "boroughs", using a network of underground tunnels.[1]

The Tunnel Rats used to do business with the Mendoza Syndicate.[2]

## Notable members

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill act as enforcers for The Tunnel Rats, punishing anyone who disrespects the group. They oppose the gangs who occasionally try and exploit the tunnel system.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The description of the Tunnel Rats is mostly reused from the original iteration in *Neon Prime* lore.

## References

[edit | edit source]

1. ↑ Mo & Krill's background - *"The Tunnel Rats, a group that help facilitate illicit trade and commerce between the boroughs thanks to a network of underground tunnels."*

## Weapon

[edit | edit source]

Tokamak has an unique gimmick for their weapon: Tokamak's ammo bar takes the form of a heat gauge which rises the longer the player fires for and lowers when Tokamak is not firing their weapon. Past a certain point, Tokamak's weapon will begin to overheat, granting increased firing speed. However, the player must be careful, because if Tokamak overheats, they will be unable to fire their gun for a few seconds.

Due to the fact that Tokamak is unfinished, the heat gauge will stay on the HUD even if the player switches to another hero.

**Curie-ous Times**

68 Damage Per Second

Falloff Range

20m  ➞ 58m

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Tokamak's model was a modified version of  Bebop's model.
- Fathom's second ability, **Breach**, is a combination of two abilities Tokamak had: Functionally, it is identical to Tokamak's **Dying Star** and its name was taken from a removed ability for Tokamak also called **Breach**.
- Raven's ultimate ability, **Revelation**, is also functionally similar to Tomamak's **Blinding Radiance**: Enemies are afflicted with debuffs and damage if they look towards them while their ability is active.

**Toxic Bullets** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Buildup Per Shot
- 3 Affected healing

- 3.1 Heroes
- 3.2 Items

- 3.2.1 Direct Heal items
- 3.2.2 Bullet Lifesteal items
- 3.2.3 Spirit Lifesteal items
- 4 Update history
- 5 Gallery
- 6 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Bleed damage can kill.
- The bleed effect is indicated by puddles of blood dropping from the player.
- Bleed damage applies or "ticks" every half-second, dealing slightly over 1.2% max health spirit damage per tick. This means that, by default, bleed applies damage six times every time it is successfully built up for 7.5% max health spirit damage.
- Bleed Damage is considered Spirit Damage and is reduced by Spirit Resist.
- The duration of the bleed is affected by the Ability Duration stat, such as from Superior Duration. The extra damage is applied proportionally. For instance, since Superior Duration adds .84 seconds to the bleed effect, the bleed will deal 2.1% extra spirit damage for a total of 9.6% max health spirit damage.
- Headshots do not affect the buildup per shot.
- Light and Heavy Melee attacks count as one full shot each.
- Bleed does not build on any structures, such as Guardians and Walkers. Mid-boss is also immune to bleed.
- Bleed *does* build on Troopers and Denizens, but deals 50% damage.
- The healing reduction only applies while the target is bleeding.
- The healing reduction stacks with other sources of healing reduction. For instance,  Healbane and Toxic Bullets will apply a healing reduction effect of 55%.
- The buildup per shot is also affected by weapon falloff, requiring more shots for the bleed to occur at further distances. Once applied, the bleed damage itself is unaffected by distance.
- For heroes with spreadshot weapons ( Abrams,  Calico,  Yamato, etc.), the listed bleed buildup applies on a shot where *every* pellet hits its target. The buildup is divided evenly between each pellet and missing one pellet will proportionally decrease buildup.
- For characters with burst-fire weapons ( Lash,  Seven, etc.), the listed bleed buildup applies for each bullet rather than each burst. Landing a full burst as Lash, for instance, will build 45.9% of bleed on a target.
- For characters with splash damage alternate fire weapons ( Viscous and  Yamato), the listed bleed buildup applies in full regardless of whether a target was hit directly or indirectly with a shot.
- Shiv's alt-fire builds bleed identically to his primary fire.

## Buildup Per Shot

[edit | edit source]

The item has a different buildup per shot depending on which hero purchased the item. The bleed only triggers on an enemy once the buildup reaches 100%, and the buildup decays back to 0 over time if the enemy has not been shot recently. Subsequent shots on a bleeding enemy (bullets or melee) refreshes the duration of the bleed.

**Transcendent Cooldown** is a Tier 4  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**. Its component,  Superior Cooldown, makes up  **3,200** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- When bought, Cooldown Reduction is applied retroactively to abilities already on cooldown.
- It reduces all item cooldowns, for both passive and active effects.
- It does not affect Charge-Up items, such as  Tankbuster and  Mercurial Magnum.

**Trapper** is an unreleased Hero in *Deadlock*, previously available in the Hero Labs gamemode.

A hard-working civil servant of the New York Municipal Coven, Trapper is ready to clock in during Maelstrom day to earn some basketball tickets.

Trapper was added to Hero Labs on November 7, 2024, and removed from the game when the mode was discontinued on August 18, 2025.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

“

An employee of the New York Municipal Coven; Trapper spends his days building Spirit Urns, luring giant rats, and capturing various invasive species from The Outer Planes.  It's not a particularly glamorous job, and he really hates working with spiders, but those Knickerbocker season tickets don't pay for themselves.

### Lore

[edit | edit source]

Trapper is fighting in the Ritual because he "volunteered to work Maelstrom day."[1]

While he hates spirit spiders[2], Trapper loves working for the Municipal Coven.[3]

Trapper wants to impress someone named Cinnamon[4], who is likely a stripper. [5]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Holliday appreciates working with Trapper because of how "normal" he is.[6]
- Calico feels like killing Trapper is lowering herself[7] and expresses total contempt for Trapper.[8]
- Holliday[9], Mirage[10], Pocket[11] and the Shopkeeper[12] respect Trapper and appreciate the work he does as part of the Municipal Coven.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Trapper's jacket used to be black when he was first added to Hero Labs on November 7, 2024. This model was updated on February 25, 2025, changing the color of Trapper's clothes and removing the spiders on his model.
- Trapper currently uses the generic Target Dummy model. His previous model, a modified version of  Pocket's original model, was removed in the Six Heroes update.

**Troopers**, also colloquially called **Creeps** or **Minions**, are common offensive units summoned by the Patron. They are the primary force for pushing lanes and  **** Soul farming throughout the game.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Super Troopers
- 1.2 Combat Stats
- 1.3 Health Regen
- 1.4 Math
- 2 Trooper types

- 2.1 Ranged Trooper
- 2.2 Melee Trooper
- 2.3 Medic Trooper
- 3 Update history
- 4 Gallery
- 5 Commands
- 6 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Troopers appear to be small humanoid automata with a large burning candle atop their head. In combat, the amount of wax on the candle directly reflects the amount of health a trooper has. There are 3 types of basic troopers: Ranged Troopers, Melee Troopers and Medic Troopers. Each trooper wave has 2 Ranged, 1 Melee and 1 Medic.

Troopers serve as the primary means to pushing lanes. The waves spawn as follows:

| Match duration | Spawn frequency |
| --- | --- |
| 0 to 20 min | 30s |
| 20 to 35 min | 25s |
| over 35 min | 20s |

Initially the waves consist of 3 Ranged Troopers and 1 Medic Trooper; after 5 minutes they become 2 Ranged, 1 Melee and 1 Medic. Troopers enter lanes by riding Ziplines in a vessel, which can be shot down to force them to drop early. Once on the ground, Troopers will attempt to move down the lane, attacking other enemy Troopers, Heroes and structures on the way.

During laning phase, Troopers are also the most reliable source of Souls. Slain Troopers will drop a Soul Orb on the ground that can be picked up by nearby ally players for 60% of the soul bounty, and release a floating Soul Orb that can be confirmed or denied by players for the remaining 40% souls. Killing a Trooper with a melee attack prevents orbs from spawning and awards 100% of the value on kill.

### Super Troopers

[edit | edit source]

Once an enemy Shrine has been destroyed, allied Troopers from that Shrine's lane (and for the Blue lane once either Shrine has been destroyed) become **Super Troopers**, gaining 60% damage and 40% health for the rest of the match. They also yield 15% less bounty when killed by enemies.

### Combat Stats

[edit | edit source]

Troopers have a complex set of resistances and vulnerabilities that change based on the game's state and their opponents.

| Enemy Type | Damage Output (DPS) | Damage Resist (%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Players | 28 | -25 |
| Troopers | 35 | 42.5 |
| Guardians | 14.4 | 0 |
| Walkers | 24 | 80 |
| Base Guardians | 80 | 67.5 |
| Shrines | 50 | 0 |
| Patron | 50 | 50 |

Note: Player damage resist is applied against Bullet Damage, but not against Melee Damage.

**Other combat stats**

- They gradually gain spirit resistance over time, reaching 20% at 25 minutes and 70% at 50 minutes.
- Troopers gain 35% damage resistance when near/in the enemy base.
- At 35 minutes, all Troopers gain +50% HP.

**Sight Range**

- Troopers have two different sight ranges:

- **Vs. NPCs:** 41m
- **Vs. Heroes:** 18m

### Health Regen

[edit | edit source]

Troopers have 7 out of combat health regen.

### Math

[edit | edit source]

Trooper bounty is divided by 60% in the ground Orb and 40% in the floating Orb, or 100% on death if killed by a melee attack.

The total Soul bounty per Trooper is equal to  **116** + ( **1.16** per min).

Additionally, they are divided among nearby ally players at the rates listed in table below:

| Players | % share to each player | Total % |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 100% | 100% |
| 2 | 54% | 108% |
| 3 | 36% | 108% |
| 4 | 25% | 100% |
| 5 | 20% | 100% |
| 6 | 16% | 96% |

## Trooper types

[edit | edit source]

### Ranged Trooper

[edit | edit source]

**Ranged Troopers** are the most common type of Trooper. They attack with a ranged weapon that has a range of **25m**, resorting to a melee if enemies get too close.

### Melee Trooper

[edit | edit source]

**Melee Troopers** are bulkier and tougher units with **400** health and a faster walk speed of **8.1** m/s. They engage enemies with a melee attack within a **3m** range. Melee Troopers only start spawning after 5 minutes.

### Medic Trooper

[edit | edit source]

A medic pack dropped by a medic trooper

**Medic Troopers,** also referred to as **Banner Troopers,** are a special type of Trooper that can heal nearby Heroes and Troopers when they are killed. They are distinguished by carrying a large banner with a health symbol.

Killing a Medic Trooper will drop a **Medic Pack** that has to be picked up by a player. It heals allies in a 35m radius, based on the following formula:

*Heal = (12% of hero's missing HP + 150 HP + 2 HP per minute) / Number of nearby heroes*

Medic Packs cannot be picked up by the Trooper's own team.

Medic Packs pickup range increases from 18m at 10 minutes to 30m at 18 minutes.

Troopers are also healed by a small amount when the Medic Pack is picked up by a player.

## Commands

[edit | edit source]

To summon Entities, in this case troopers (requires sv_cheats 1):

npc_create [unit_name|npc_class_name] [name of npc (optional) ] [addon type (optional) ] [name of addon (optional) ]

To summon specific troopers, use the following as unit names:

trooper_melee, trooper_nano etc.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- There's an unused Trooper model in the game files labeled **Trooper_Jetpack**, which has flying animations. The Jetpack Trooper was also present in *Neon Prime*.

- There's another unused Trooper model in the game files labeled **trooper_siege**, which has a rocket launcher.
- Before the Old Gods, New Blood update, both teams' Troopers were candle-shaped. The weapon carried by Ranged and Medic Troopers was shaped like a candle snuffer.

# Unit

**Units**, also known as **NPCs** or **Non-Playable Characters**, are any entities in *Deadlock* which are not directly controlled by the players.

## Structures

[edit | edit source]

**Structures** or **Objectives** are large Units belonging to each team. They do not respawn.

- Guardians
- Walkers
- Shrines
- Patron

## Creeps

[edit | edit source]

Creeps are Units that respawn, either in waves or after a specific time.

- Troopers
- Denizens
- Mid-Boss

## Hero-Created Units

[edit | edit source]

Units created by Heroes.

- Graves'  Ghouls
- McGinnis'  Mini Turrets
- Rem's  Lil Helpers

# United States of America

“

Next week will mark the 5 year anniversary of South Ixia officially joining the United States as its 52nd state.

— The Newscaster

**The United States of America** is a country on Earth in which the Cursed Apple is located.

## Description

[edit | edit source]

The United States is composed of 52 states. The 50th State is the Island of Cadenza,[1] the 51st is Puerto Rico,[2] and the 52nd is South Ixia.[3] Other known states include New York, Wyoming,[4] Massachusetts,[5][6] Illinois,[7] Pennsylvania[8] and Wisconsin.[9]

There are at least 2 known Astral Gates located in US territory: New York and Puerto Rico.

The OSIC is an organization within the US government.

The US government is sending aid to Ixia as part of their military campaign, drawing opposition from the Friends of Humanity.[10]

The US government is negotiating a sale of a part of Wyoming with the Djinn.[4][11]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Due to the divergences in the *Deadlock* timeline, it is currently unknown if Hawaii and Alaska are US states, as they joined the Union in the year 1959 in the real world.

# Universal Tech

*This article is part of the Deadlock Movement Wiki.*

“

Gotta be slippery in this business.

— Vyper

**Universal Tech** is movement tech that more than one character in the game can execute. These techniques are usually executable by most or all of the cast, though some involve specific interactions with a handful of characters.

Note: Some movement tech articles use source units per second (u/s) instead of meters per second. Source units in *Deadlock* are equivalent to inches, and thus can be converted to meters at a rate of 39,37:1. The player's speed in units can be viewed with the console command *cl_showpos 1*.

Below is a list of all universal techniques currently in the game:

- Walking

- Sprinting
- Stamina
- Dashing

- Strafe Dashing
- Dash Jumping
- Dash Sliding
- Short Dash Crouch Cancelling
- Instant Air Dash
- Ag2 Dashing
- Jumping

**Unstoppable** is a Tier 4  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**. Its component,  Debuff Reducer, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Interactions with Crowd-Control
- 3 Update history
- 4 Gallery
- 5 Trivia
- 6 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Unstoppable is not usable when the player loses control of their character, such as when asleep or stunned. Instead, it should be used in anticipation of these abilities to prevent them from working.
- Status Effects such as Anti-heal and Damage Debuffs (such as those applied from  Inhibitor and  Silencer) are ***NOT*** suppressed.
- Channelled abilities such as  Dynamo's  Singularity will affect the hero if Unstoppable's active ends while the ability is still ongoing.
- Unstoppable's active ability does not prevent damage from enemies, even if it prevents the negative effects.
- Although not explicitly mentioned in its description, the usage of **Unstoppable** also grants the user immunity to the Interrupt status effect.
- Unstoppable is not removed by  Cursed Relic and blocks all of it's effects, including the removal of non-ultimate buffs.

## Interactions with Crowd-Control

[edit | edit source]

- Crushing Fists

- Lightning Scroll
- Vortex Web

- Walker - Stomp
- Zipline knockdown stun

The stun induced from a parry cannot be reduced.

This effect helps mitigate crowd-control by shortening stuns' durations, allowing the hero to recover more quickly.

Note: Unstoppable *does* make the player immune to the effects listed above if activated before the effects are applied. The player can still activate Unstoppable while under the effect of debuffs that don't prevent item usage (i.e. not stunned, slept, cursed etc.).

# Updates

“

It's time to change the world.

— Warden

An **Update** is a new version of the build of the game that adds and adjusts content. Said content typically includes new or adjusted game modes, balance changes, and bug fixes. *Deadlock* currently gets updated several times a week, and not all changes are recorded in patch notes. This page lists updates mentioned on the Official Deadlock forum, and some notable unlisted changes discovered by players. Possible undocumented changes may also be identified by reviewing GitHub diffs from the GameTracking-Deadlock repository maintained by SteamDB. Update times are based on the Pacific Standard Time zone (PST) of Valve Corporation's headquarters in Bellevue, Washington.

From August 1, 2024, to December 6, 2024, the game followed a schedule in which a major update was released once every two weeks. On January 8, 2025, it was announced that this schedule was dropped in favor of having more time between major updates to allow for better testing and additional internal development time.[1]

*Deadlock* is currently in a closed beta state.[2]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Vampiric Burst appears to have previously been named "Surging Power", as many hero voice lines for it are named "use_surging_power" and heroes will often say it when Vampiric Burst is activated.

- Additionally, Lash's in-game voice lines for Vampiric Burst are "lash_use_surging_power", while another set of unused lines named "lash_use_vampiric_burst" also exist.
- Venator's  Ira Domini and  Gutshot T3 heavy melee deal +5 damage to enemies with Vampiric Burst active.

# Vasili Zorin

**Vasili Zorin** is a *Deadlock* developer. He is best known for his work as a concept artist on *Sunset Overdrive* and *Overwatch*.

Vasili was the character designer of *Neon Prime*.[1] It is believed that he still works on *Deadlock* as a character designer and concept artist.

In a January 2024 interview, Vasili said he was working on a then-unannounced project with Icefrog.[2]

“

I'll drive a stake through their heart!

**Venator** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He doesn't walk the righteous path, he blazes the trail so that others may do so safely. His biggest challenge is knowing which weapon to use first. Firing a Consecrating Grenade into the fray softens up his enemies and keeps them from restoring health, and his Hex-Lined Snap Trap scatters across the ground to lock them in place. A Gutshot from his shotgun will knock back enemies who get too close, and when the time is right, Ira Domini will rid the world of evil once and for all.

A vigilante monster hunter, Father Quinn Rourke represents the righteous wrath and fury of the Venators of Saint Benedict. Sent by his superiors at the Vatican, the Venator has been designated a mission: to annihilate the evil brewing in New York.

Venator was released on February 5, 2026 as the fourth winner of the Old Gods, New Blood update contest.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Venator/Lore** for more story content.*

“

The Venators of St. Benedict are a Vatican-sanctioned order whose members are deployed to regions with a high concentration of supernatural predators.   Few in number, their modus operandi is to observe, identify, and exterminate. They are methodical, they are precise, and once they identify a threat to the flock they are relentless.

But even amongst those who are called The Sword Of St. Benedict, one stands apart from the others.  A man whose hardened heart has allowed him to pay terrible prices in the name of the greater good... and he has once again been dispatched to New York.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- "Venator" means "hunter" in Latin.
- Venator's weapon is named after the Bible passage Jeremiah 51:20: "Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms".
- One of Venator's voice lines for upgrading **Gutshot**, "I long for the day when this will be a plowshare" references the phase "beating swords into plowshares" which comes from the Bible passage Isaiah 2:4.
- His ultimate ability, "Ira Domini", translates to "Wrath of the Lord" in Latin.
- Venator was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidently leaked on stream in May 2025.[1] A playable version of Venator was added to the files in the Shop Rework Update. A new Venator portrait was leaked in a work-in-progress hero select screen posted on 4chan in July 2025. On 20th January 2026, Venator was teased in the Hideout with a thurible on a bookshelf.
- Before he was named "Quinn", Venator was named "Cain" during development before his release.[2][3][4]
- Venator originally had the Shopkeeper voice actor as a temp VO, who made self-aware jokes about his role. The female temp voice (currently on Boho) called him "the bodega guy".[5]
- Prior to the Six New Heroes Update, Venator had an ability called "Potent Vapors", a channel which would heal Venator and grant him movement slow resist at the cost of him being unable to attack throughout its channel. This ability was replaced with Consecrating Grenade.

- Additionally, prior to the Old Gods, New Blood update, Venator used to have an ability called "Penace and Retribution", a passive that would grant Venator stacking bullet and spirit resistances as he took sustained damage. This ability was replaced with Hex-Lined Snap Trap.
- "Blessing Ammunition in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Venator in the Hideout.
- Venator's selection voice line "Ours is not to question what is necessary. Ours is to have the will to do whatever it takes" is likely a reference to Alfred Tennyson's poem *The Charge of the Light Brigade*:  "Theirs not to make reply, Theirs not to reason why, Theirs but to do and die".
- Venator had the largest winning margin in the Old Gods, New Blood hero contest, winning by an 11% difference over  Celeste.[6]
- Venator's weapon appears to be loosely based on a Heckler & Koch MP5, which officially entered service in 1966 but was designed as early as 1964.[7] Additionally its under-barrel grenade launcher has been decorated to resemble a typical Ave Maria "Votive candle"[8] commonly found in Catholic home altars. This is also coupled with some Rosary beads[9] in place of a sling harness.

The Venators of St. Benedict are a Vatican-sanctioned order whose members are deployed to regions with a high concentration of supernatural predators.   Few in number, their modus operandi is to observe, identify, and exterminate. They are methodical, they are precise, and once they identify a threat to the flock they are relentless.

But even amongst those who are called The Sword Of St. Benedict, one stands apart from the others.  A man whose hardened heart has allowed him to pay terrible prices in the name of the greater good... and he has once again been dispatched to New York.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Venator's mission and motivation in the ritual is to kill the Patrons.[1][2] He's willing to die to achieve his mission.[3]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Venator's real name is Quinn Rourke.[4][5] He is commonly referred to by his title, "Father",[5][6] which is ordinary for Catholic priests.

There are less than 24 active Venators,[7] though more have been killed in the past.[8] The Roman numeral "48" under Venator's typography may indicate that he is the 48th Venator. While there are multiple Venators, they usually work alone.[9]

Venator's accent is Irish.

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Venator showcases that he's willing to do whatever he can for the greater good, burdening himself with the sins he commits for the sake of others.[10][11] His zealous behavior often causes him to be called "angry" and "unhinged".[12] He does, however, judge people based on their actions rather than their appearances or species.[13]

Venator refers to himself as a Carnifex, a Latin word for executioner.[14]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

The Venators of St. Benedict have a friendly rivalry with the Baxter Society.[15] Venator respects the Baxter Society, though he doesn't always agree with them.[16]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Grey Talon

[edit | edit source]

Venator respects Grey Talon, referring to him by his first name and promising to pray for his deceased family.[17][18]

While on opposing teams, Grey Talon wishes they were fighting on the same side.[19]

### Calico

[edit | edit source]

Venator knew Calico from when she was in the Baxter Society, but loathes her now that she's an assassin.[20]

Venator believes that, for the right price, Calico would be willing to kill Ava.[21]

When killing Calico, Venator mentions that it was "for Grey Talon".[22] He also references the 30 pieces of silver that Judas received for betraying Jesus when killing Calico, presumably referring to Calico leaving the Baxter Society.[23]

### Agent Marlowe

[edit | edit source]

Venator is a friend of Marlowe and calls him a "bastard".[24]

### Holliday

[edit | edit source]

Venator prays with Holliday before the ritual to try and help heal her trauma from the Macomb massacre. While it doesn't work, Holliday appreciates Venator for trying.[25]

Venator also warns Holliday to tend her pain and anger before it consumes her.[26]

-Abrams

-Shiv(?)

-Drifter(?)

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- As a hunter of the wicked, Venator showcases righteous anger towards malevolent creatures and objects, including Abrams' Tome,[27] Graves' lich hand,[28] and Oathkeeper.[29]
- Akin to Silver, Venator doesn't believe in Shiv's change of heart, waiting for him to slip up and ruin his "charade".[30][31] He expresses surprise with Grey Talon's choice of replacement as his protégé, trusting that Shiv should be dead and warning Grey Talon that, if Shiv strays from the path of redemption, the Venators of St. Benedict will come for him.[32]
- Venator prays with Bebop for the sake of Ms. Shelly,[33] and prays with Holliday to try and make her feel better about The Troubadour's massacre in Macomb.[25]
- Venator believes Paige's brother, Bryce, is beyond saving, expressing remorse that she's "thrown away her life to save someone who doesn't deserve it."[34][35]
- Venator and Silver get along with each other, planning to go drink whiskey together after the ritual.[36][37]
- The Archmother and The Hidden King know Venator sees them as his enemy, but each try to convince Venator to work with them to kill the other Patron.[38][39]
- Drifter has killed other Venators before,[40] though he had higher expectations for the playable Venator.[41] If they're on the same team, Venator promises to kill Drifter after the ritual.[42]
- Paradox was expecting Venator to come after her at some point, implying the Paradox Organisation has robbed the Vatican before.[43]
- Vyper likes Venator's voice.[44]

# Vent

*For Air Vents, see Jump pad.*

A vent in blue lane.
A subway station under blue lane, accessible by vents.

**Vents** are small shortcut passages in the map that lead to a network of underground tunnels connecting different locations.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Known Bugs
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Vents are only accessible by specific characters, and they cannot enter while in combat (taking or dealing damage) or while carrying the Soul Urn.

- The vent entrances have a grill as a visual indicator to players within 10 metres if these are inaccessible at the given moment.

The following heroes can access vents:

- Rem, when crouching
- Calico in  Ava form
- Mo & Krill during  Burrow

Grey Talon's  Guided Owl can also enter vents, if the player manages to enter at the correct angle without hitting any walls. It can also enter and exit the tunnels through the gap over the fence in the subway room next to Mid-Boss.

While in the tunnels, characters gain a **70%** boost to their Move Speed. Sprint speed is not multiplied by the tunnel boost.

If a hero requires an ability to enter vents and the ability duration runs out inside a vent or tunnel too small to walk/crouch on, the effect is different depending on the hero:

- For  Calico, she can activate the transformation and be pushed to the nearest walkable area. If she doesn't transform, she will stay as Ava and start rapidly taking damage, and transform back when she exits the space.
- For  Mo & Krill, they will instantly exit Burrow in one of the nearest walkable spaces either inside or outside the tunnels. {Whether they are pushed to the inside or outside seems to be inconsistent.}

Crates can be found inside tunnels, and cockroaches that can be killed for  **1**.

## Known Bugs

[edit | edit source]

- A player without vent-accessing abilities may accidentally get stuck in the tunnels by glitching through geometry. In this case, the only way to exit is by opening the console with F7 and using the "killme" command to die and respawn. Using the "Unstick" button does not change the player's location.

## Gallery

[edit | edit source]

- Deadlock vents system layered with the regular map

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Due to the size of the tunnels, crates found inside them are smaller than normal crates.

“

Fighting me has consequences.

**Victor** is a Hero in *Deadlock* who walks the line between life and death. Victor has learned to harness pain, shocking himself with Jumpstart to get his adrenaline rushing and his faulty heart pumping. He welcomes incoming damage with open (albeit mismatched) arms, channeling it into his Pain Battery and granting enemies a taste of the pain he endures. Get too close and risk getting caught in his Aura of Suffering, but hey, at least you'll be suffering together. And just when you think you've taken him down, he'll piece himself back together and live again!

After waking up in a mortuary table with no memories, Victor wants nothing more than to find out who made him and from whom he is made of.

Victor was released on August 29, 2025 as the final hero of the Six New Heroes update.

Notes

- Purges all debuffs when triggered. Victor is invincible and unable to move or act during channel.
- If  Aura of Suffering is active when Shocking Reanimation is triggered, it will turn itself off during the channel, then automatically reactivate itself when Victor revives. This resets Aura's damage ramp-up.
- Shocking Reanimation is not affected by Silence.
- Attacks that trigger Shocking Reanimation will not register any deaths/kills/assists in the HUD. They *will,* however, trigger any and all "on hero kill" and "on assist" effects/stacks for the would-be killer and/or assistant(s).
- If Victor has  Cheat Death or a Rejuvenator credit, their effects are only triggered if Shocking Reanimation is on cooldown.

- The only exception is for  Shiv's  Killing Blow, which will trigger both Shocking Reanimation and Cheat Death at the same time.
- The "non-lethal" damage-over-time dealt by  Affliction will nevertheless trigger Shocking Reanimation if it brings Victor down to 1 health. It is unclear whether or not this interaction is intentional.
