## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Victor's name is a reference to Victor Frankenstein; the creator of Frankenstein's monster in Mary Shelly's 1818 novel *Frankenstein*.
- Victor's appearance and attractiveness are likely also inspired by Frankenstein's monster's description in the original novel, quote: *"I had selected his features as beautiful. Beautiful! Great God! His skin scarcely covered his work of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing."* [2]
- Victor was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidentally leaked on stream in May 2025, originally named **Frank**.[3] Victor's model was also leaked when a game tester from Deadlock's private build accidentally posted a bug report about Victor to *Deadlock's* public forums in July 2025.
- "Brooding in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Victor in the Hideout.
- Victor has heterochromia. This is likely due to the fact that he is a patchwork of different body parts and they're two different people's eyes.
- The barbed wire wrapped around Victor's left arm will glow with electricity when Pain Battery is ready to be used.

This page is under construction. To avoid edit conflicts, please consult the edit history and the talk page.

A lot of people spend their whole lives wondering who they really are. For Victor, this existential question is made more complicated as he woke up on a mortuary table with no knowledge of his creator, why he was made, and whom he is made of.

Now searching the five boroughs for answers, Victor is hoping to find someone who can identify any part of him.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Biography
- 1.2 Personality
- 1.3 Information
- 2 Character Interactions
- 3 References
- 4 Navigation

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Victor is made out of dead body parts.[1] Though he has been searching for a while, he has yet to find the origins of any of his body parts.[2]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Victor's in constant chronic pain, with the only relief being from  The Cube.[3] He's often seen by the other heroes as sad or pitiable.[4]

Victor's willing to do anything for answers on his origins.[5]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Because Victor doesn't know where pieces of his body come from, he hasn't replaced or discarded any limbs.[6] It's implied that Victor's physical condition is deteriorating, and his left arm keeps falling off.[7][6]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Victor is considered attractive. Infernus calls him "a pretty good looking corpse",[8] and Silver refers to him as the "prettiest corpse on Manhattan".[9] Paige tells Victor never to put on a shirt,[10] and Mina offers to properly sew his body together if he'll work as a clothing model at one of her shows.[11]

- Ivy attempts to ask Victor out to dinner.[12]
- Victor often asks other characters for any leads on his origins. He asks Mo & Krill if he can search the New York sewers to see if any body parts down there match his own.[13] He also asks Dynamo where Columbia College gets their cadavers for their medical program.[14] Victor asks Abrams if any of his past cases included "a mad genius who lost one of his creations".[15]
- Victor asks Abrams for help with uncovering his past.[16]
- Victor wishes Pocket luck with their problems.[17]
- Victor and Kelvin promised each other that they'd stick together, as they're both walking corpses.[18][19]
- Lady Geist suggests that Victor should see her grandson, Johann Jr., to get him fixed.[7]

- Lady Geist calls Johann her son. It's unclear if this is a mistake or a lie by Lady Geist to hide her age.
- Mina offers to stitch up Victor's wounds if he stars in one of her fashion shows.[20]
- Infernus and Kelvin tell Victor to focus on his future instead of his past.[21][22]
- Ivy and Paige have offered to help Victor with his problems.[23][24]
- Bebop, Grey Talon, Kelvin, Krill, Mirage and Vindicta wish Victor luck in uncovering his past.[4]
- Seven believes Victor doesn't know a thing about "real" suffering.[25]
- Yamato is offended by Victor's existence.[26][27]
- Bebop has invited Victor to see Ms. Shelly.[28]
- The Doorman has invited Victor to the Baroness Hotel.[29]

“

If they don't have an Achilles' heel, I'll make one.

**Vindicta** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. She is a mobile and powerful marksman, engaging and picking off her targets from a distance. Using her Crow Familiar to initiate fights by bleeding her targets, Vindicta may launch into Flight to keep her distance from enemies and tether them with a Stake in the ground while targeting them with her powerful rifle. Enemies that are near-death should fear her ability to Assassinate at long-range with a devastating sniper shot.

A girl who was accused of witchcraft and killed by John Hathorne during the Salem Witch Trials of the 1600s, Vindicta returned to this world during the first Maelstrom. Seeking to protect her fellow supernatural entities, Vindicta is waging a war against the Neo-inquisitorial "Friends of Humanity".

A victim of John Hathorne during the Salem Witch Trials, Vindicta got a second chance of life when her spirit was brought back to the mortal plane during the first Maelstrom (the event that introduced the supernatural to the public at large).

Waging a one ghost war against "The Friends of Humanity", a neo inquisition formed by Hathorne's descendants; Vindicta looks to keep the supernatural safe from Hathorne's ilk, and she isn't afraid to stack as many bodies as needed to do it.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Vindicta's motivation in the ritual is to wipe out John Hathorne's bloodline and the Friends of Humanity.[1][2][3][4] Her main goal seems to be getting revenge on Hathorne's bloodline, with the destruction of the Friends of Humanity being a side benefit.[5]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Vindicta says she uses her given name.[6] Puritans in the 17th Century were known to give unusual names to their children, as a way of honoring their religion.[7][8]

Vindicta says she was a child who was "unjustly condemned" during the Salem Witch Trials.[9] John Hathorne, who's mentioned in Vindicta's background, was known in the actual Salem Witch Trials for questioning accusers and the accused in trial, often leaving the accused guilty.[10]

Vindicta has been dead for roughly 200 years[11] before returning to life during the first Maelstrom (50 years before the events of the game).[12]

Vindicta's main target is the current leader of the Friends of Humanity, also named John Hathorne, who is a descendant of the original Hathorne who killed her.[13][14] Vindicta has killed John Hathorne's brother while he was on a speedboat,[15] and assassinated someone else during the Boston Marathon.[16]

Vindicta's exploits have been told about in Ixia. According to  Apollo, Vindicta is called *"Hasha Vogali",* which is Ixian for "Death's Whisper".[17]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Vindicta says she's not a witch because, in her eyes, she doesn't have wants or dreams: only a lust for revenge.[18]

After returning from the dead, Vindicta says she was "lost" for a while before finding her purpose of revenge.[19] Despite being consumed by revenge, Vindicta ultimately sees her actions as her "saving life".[20][21]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Grey Talon

[edit | edit source]

Vindicta and Grey Talon have hunted the Friends of Humanity together and regard each other as friends.[22][23][24]

Vindicta calls Grey Talon by his first name and believes that, if her father was like Grey Talon, she would never have died during the Salem Witch Trials.[25]

-Haze(?)

-Apollo(?)

-Ivy(?)

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Vindicta is referred to as Goody Proctor by  Mo & Krill.[26]
- Vindicta believes  Ivy is naive and warns her that, if she doesn't smarten up soon, someone she cares about will be hurt.[27]
- Haze warns Vindicta to "quit while she's ahead", because murdering John Hathorne will "galvanize" the Friends of Humanity.[28] She calls Vindicta a "domestic terrorist".[29]
- Apollo commends Vindicta for her war against the Friends of Humanity, although he dislikes her dishonorable tactics.[30][31]
- Graves wishes she could help Vindicta with her problems.[32][33]
- Abrams,[34]  Kelvin,[35]  Paige[36] and  Warden[37] are sympathetic to Vindicta's cause.
- Abrams,[38]  Billy,[39]  Holliday,[40]  Mina,[41]  Wraith[42] and  Yamato[43] point out that Vindicta doesn't wear shoes.

- Rem likes that Vindicta also doesn't wear shoes.[44]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

### Neon Prime - Hornet

[edit | edit source]

Vindicta was named **Hornet** in *Neon Prime*. Hornet was voiced by Jeannie Tirado, who currently voices  Ivy.

Update history

Sounds

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| March 10, 2026 | - Fixed not gaining bonus damage if a proc bonus was the killing blow. |
| March 6, 2026 | - Fire Rate no longer scales with Spirit Power - Bullet damage now scales with spirit power (0.022) - Ammo reduced from 22 to 19 - Bullet Velocity increased from 557 to 660 - Stake damage reduced from 55 to 40 - Stake damage spirit scaling increased from 0.37 to 0.5 - Stake projectile speed increased from 20m/s to 25m/s - Stake T1 changed from "-35% Fire Rate" to "+65 Damage" - Stake T3 Tether Duration increased from +0.5s to +0.75s - Stake T3 capture radius increased from +1m to +2m - Flight now allows you to use melee - Flight now allows parry to be used - Flight now grants you +50% Item Cast Range - Flight spirit damage scaling reduced from 0.22 to 0.18 - Flight duration reduced from 15s to 13s - Flight T2 duration increased from +8s to +10s - Flight T3 Spirit Damage Per Bullet reduced from 12.6 to 10 - Flight T3 now increases spirit scaling by 0.1 - Flight T3 now also refreshes duration on hero kill - Crow Familiar now releases a swarm of crows in a cone forward, hitting all enemies along the path - Crow Familiar debuff duration no longer scales with spirit power - Crow Familiar debuff duration increased from 4s to 5s - Crow Familiar bleed damage reduced from 2.7% to 2.2% - Crow Familiar damage increased from 37 to 40 - Crow Familiar cooldown increased from 28s to 32s - Crow Familiar T1 changed from "Ricochet up to 2 times" to "Reduces healing by -35%" - Crow Familiar T2 now also increase bleed damage by +0.5% - Crow Familiar T3 now also increases debuff duration by 2s - Assassinate while scoped no longer un-scopes when using items - Assassinate now has a 4s buffer on impact for bonus credit - Assassinate while scoped now plays a sound for you when the it is fully charged - Assassinate weapon damage bonus increased from 5% to 6% |
| January 30, 2026 | - Stake Tether Length no longer increases when Capture Radius increases. - Assassinate now grants +5% Weapon Damage per kill rather than Bonus Souls. - Assassinate T3 now provides an additional +4% Weapon Damage per kill (retroactive). |
| January 22, 2026 | - **(Undocumented)**  Lightning Scroll now procs on  Assassinate |
| December 16, 2025 | - Assassinate T2 reduced from +90 Max Bonus Damage to 80. |
| December 3, 2025 | - Fix for FOV "pop" in  Vindicta's  Assassination |
| October 2, 2025 | - Base bullet damage increased from 11.4 to 11.8 - Flight duration increased from 13s to 15s - Flight T2 increased from 7s to 8s - Flight spirit damage scaling increased from 0.19 to 0.22 - Assassinate bonus damage spirit scaling increased from 1.4 to 1.7 - Assassinate cooldown reduced from 60s to 50s |
| September 4, 2025 | - Stake no longer has a smaller tether range than capture range (6m to 9m, no longer pulls you) - Stake duration reduced from 2s to 1.75s. - Stake slow increased from 30% to 40%. - Flight duration increased from 12s to 13s. - Flight spirit damage increased from 9 to 10. - Flight T2 increased from +6s to +7s. - Flight T3 increased from +11 Spirit Damage to +14. - Crow Familiar debuff duration reduced from 6s to 4s. - Crow Familiar debuff duration spirit scaling reduced from 0.022 to 0.013. - Crow Familiar bleed per second increased from 2.15% to 2.7%. - Crow Familiar T2 reduced from -16s Cooldown to -12s. |
| August 18, 2025 | - New updated model. - **(Undocumented)** Updated VO pass |
| July 29, 2025 | - Crow[*sic*]The preceding quote has been reproduced verbatim and is not a transcription error. T1 bounce no longer bounces off of objectives. - Stake T3 reduced from +2m to +1m. |
| May 8, 2025 | - Minor rework on animation set. - Assassinate: Fixed  Vindicta  Assassinate zoom in sound triggering twice. - Fixed issues that were preventing  Yamato,  Vindicta, and  Pocket desperation lines from playing. - Fix  Vindicta  flight[*sic*]The preceding quote has been reproduced verbatim and is not a transcription error. and  Wraith  Full Auto spirit damage not working if the enemy has a barrier. |
| April 17, 2025 | - Crow Familiar Cooldown increased from 26s to 28s. - Crow Familiar T3 Spirit and Bullet Resist Reduction reduced from -12% to -8%. |
| April 4, 2025 | - Crow Familiar duration spirit scaling reduced from 0.03 to 0.024. - Crow Familiar Health Drain reduced from 3% to 2.3%. |
| February 25, 2025 | - Fixed getting stuck zoomed in if you tried to use  Assassinate while getting stunned or silenced. - Updated vo - largely remastering pass, but some new content. |
| January 27, 2025 | - Bullet damage reduced from 11.7 to 11.4. - Crow[*sic*]The preceding quote has been reproduced verbatim and is not a transcription error. projectile speed reduced from 4750 to 4250. - Assassinate T2 reduced from +120 to +110. |
| January 19, 2025 | - Movespeed reduced from 9 to 8. - Bullet Velocity reduced from 810 to 740. |

“

It's funny because I'm basically immortal.

**Viscous** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He is a vexing opponent with versatile goo abilities, a psychic sea anemone with an ectoplasmic goo body. He can Splatter his foes with a large ball of goo and Puddle Punch both allies and enemies to knock them around, while encasing himself or allies in a Cube of goo for protection. For maximum disruption, Viscous can morph into a large Goo Ball and bounce off of walls and enemies alike.

Viscous is a psychic sea anemone that fears a dark, dangerous predator that prowls the depths under the Bermuda Triangle. He reached the surface in a body built from ectoplasmic goo; his mission to summon the Patrons to protect his home in the Deep.

Viscous was added to the roster on August 1, 2024.

## Weapon

[edit | edit source]

**Deep Sea Interpreter**

Medium Range

Projectile

49 Damage Per Second

Falloff Range

20m  ➞ 58m

Deep Sea Interpreter has an alternate fire mode, which releases a larger projectile that explodes in a small area of effect upon collision, or after flying for long enough. This alt-fire takes 5 ammo rounds per shot and deals 42+0.36 damage on a direct hit.The alt-fire mode can be used even with fewer than 5 rounds of ammo, and still deals its full damage.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Viscous/Lore** for more story content.*

“

The Bermuda Triangle was never a myth, it was a shadowline nexus deep underneath the Atlantic Ocean.  For the most part, the things that escaped this astral gate were benign (like Nessie), but now something dark and predatory known only as The Adversary hunts the seas... and ocean denizens are scared to death.

One of those inhabitants, a psychic sea anemone, wants to do something about it.  Summoning an ectoplasmic goo body to traverse the surface, Viscous is desperately trying to summon the Patrons in order to keep The Deep safe from the horror that lurks below.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Viscous' current model is a modified version of Kelvin's old model from *Neon Prime*.

- A work-in-progress alternate model can be found in the files, labeled **Viscous v2**, in which he is a large man with a coral arm and an octopus-like creature in his head.
- A new model labeled **Viscous_tourist**, in which he wears shorts, sunglasses, an orange cap and a portable camera, has also been referenced in the files and leaked in images in June 2025. The current icon for Goo Ball shows the camera, glove and boot from this new model.
- In *Neon Prime*, Viscous was a pufferfish in a suit, instead of a sea anemone.
- Viscous' head was changed from black to green in the 2024-09-26 Update, because his old icon was easily confused with Dynamo.
- "Wishing the Hideout was The Cube" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Viscous in the Hideout.
- Developer Hopoo has joked on Discord that the  Vortex Web squid and Viscous "went to the same high school".[4]

“

I am not a pile of goo. I'm merely piloting a pile of goo.

The Bermuda Triangle was never a myth, it was a shadowline nexus deep underneath the Atlantic Ocean.  For the most part, the things that escaped this astral gate were benign (like Nessie), but now something dark and predatory known only as The Adversary hunts the seas... and ocean denizens are scared to death.

One of those inhabitants, a psychic sea anemone, wants to do something about it.  Summoning an ectoplasmic goo body to traverse the surface, Viscous is desperately trying to summon the Patrons in order to keep The Deep safe from the horror that lurks below.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Viscous is innocent and optimistic, eager to learn about the surface world and make new friends, and likes to compliment others.[1] However, he takes his mission to stop the Adversary very seriously, as noted by  Seven.[2] He believes that others underestimate him and the problems of the Deep.[3][4]

Viscous is commonly referred to as a "tourist".[5][6][7][8] While on the surface, he wants to watch South Pacific,[9] free his "brothers" from New York's aquariums,[10] try climbing some stairs in his goo body,[11] and visit a variety of locations in New York, including Staten Island, Long Island, New Jersey and Secaucus.[12]

Viscous enjoys violence, which surprises him.[13][14]

Viscous likes people-watching.[15]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Viscous can't read.[16]

The Cube is a protoplasmic cube.[17] The Cube nullifies all pain, even for characters like Victor.[18] Viscous doesn't question how the Cube works, even when it can heal non-organic bodies like Bebop's.[19] Viscous spends time in the Cube whenever he feels sad.[20]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Haze

[edit | edit source]

Haze takes Viscous and his problems seriously.[4] She wants to know more about the Adversary in case more creatures like it come through the Deep's astral gate.[21]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Viscous offers the Cube to Ms. Shelly and Grey Talon.[22][20]
- Viscous likes Holliday's hat and wants to wear it.[23]
- Viscous thinks Seven and Warden are scary.[24][25]
- When  Seven learns about Viscous' mission, he admits there's more to Viscous than he expected.[2]
- Abrams,[26] Bebop, Holliday, Lash, Mina, Mo & Krill and Paradox refer to Viscous as "goo boy".[27]
- Grey Talon offers to have The Baxter Society help Viscous defeat the Adversary should they fail the ritual.[28]
- Holliday mistakes Viscous' home, The Deep, for the American Deep South. She asks if he's from Mobile, Alabama.[29]
- Lady Geist and  McGinnis want to salvage some of Viscous' goo for themselves.[30][31]
- Calico is interested in Viscous' suit.[32]
- Paige wants to take Viscous home and give him a hug.[33]
- Infernus advises Viscous to decline  Wraith's offers to play cards.[34]
- Apollo accidentally invites Viscous to one of his father's galas.[35]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

Neon Prime
In Neon Prime, Viscous looked the same as the first version of his current model, but he had an icon in which he was depicted with a pufferfish inside his head.

# Viscous/Movement

Overview

Movement

List of known movement tech for **Viscous**.

Viscous has a litany of abilities that can aid in his movement. Excepting his first ability, *Splatter*, all of his abilities can directly move him, allies or enemies or have some interaction that can move him.

Viscous' various movement techniques can be comboed into each other, and sometimes sequences do not have names, and are instead referred to as the combination of the movement techniques seen below. When viewing a clip, please keep in mind that we do not aim to directly name every interaction and movement combination available.

## Puddle Punch

[edit | edit source]

*Puddle Punch* is Viscous' third ability, in which he materialises a goo fist that deals Light Melee damage. *Puddle Punch* is one of the few abilities in the game to directly displace you and enemies with velocity; in this regard, it can be considered similar to the Soldier's rockets in Team Fortress 2.

When enemies parry *Puddle Punch*, damage and knockback is negated. This also counts as a parry against Viscous; items such as the Vitality item Rebuttal procs on a successful parry on *Puddle Punch*.

When casting there is a short delay before the fist comes out, in which the fist has not materialised and is a goo puddle. This gives an audio cue, which can allow the enemy to parry *Puddle Punch*.

The knockback that *Puddle Punch* gives varies based on the distance from the centre of the fist; the closer you are to the centre, the more velocity you will have afterwards and your resulting trajectory will align with the direction of the fist. When hit towards the edges, your trajectory may vary from side to side, and velocity might be transferred from forwards velocity to sidewards velocity.

*Puddle Punch* affects Viscous, his allies and the opposing team; this can be used for advantageous movement for him and his team or to directly displace his enemies.

*Puddle Punch* can be cast on any surface in the game. This includes the skybox and incredibly small pieces of geometry, such as the curbs on the sides of lanes. *Puddle Punch* will always materialise perpendicular to the targeted surface.

### Puddle Punch Boosting

[edit | edit source]

Intentionally being hit by *Puddle Punch* to displace yourself is called ***Puddle Punch* Boosting**. *Puddle Punch* Boosting is a broad term meant to describe the act of displacing yourself, and encompasses a litany of smaller, more refined techniques.

The basic *Puddle Punch* Boost is timing your *Puddle Punch* so that it hits you when you are airborne; by casting on a vertical wall then jumping, you can gain significant velocity; depending on your positioning relative to the fist, this can be upwards velocity or forwards velocity.

*Puddle Punch* Boosting can be executed while in *Goo Ball* form. When this happens, this is called *Goo Ball* Punching.

| Wall Punch Dashing |  |
| --- | --- |
| Wall Punch Dashing |  |
| Tech Type: | Character Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Inputs: | Dash → *Puddle Punch* |

### Wall Punch Dashing

[edit | edit source]

When Dashing, your velocity is intended to be set to a set sequence; this means that normally, Dashing disregards all previous momentum; this makes it a generally bad option for moving fast around the map in all situations.

When being boosted by *Puddle Punch* while Dashing, your *Puddle Punch* will "stack" velocity with (i.e. add to) the velocity of the Dash. This results in a consistent forward velocity of *1430±10* u/s.

Since *Puddle Punch* affects your teammates, other players on your team can also use Dash *Puddle Punch*; this can set up gank parties and large escapes. However, your enemies can also use Dash *Puddle Punch* for their own movement (they do still take the regular damage).

**Wall Punch Dashing** is considered a staple of advanced Viscous movement, and usually sets up movement sequences. The technique is useful in all stages of the game; during laning phase you can effectively move around the map quicker for ganks; during mid-game this can lead to fast rotates and easy chases, and during late-game this can be used as an escape tool with your team.

### Air Vent Puddle Boost

[edit | edit source]

By timing *Puddle Punch* as to boost you when you walk onto an Air Vent, you can stack the momentum from both to gain massive vertical momentum and travel long distances.

If you are in ball form, you travel further and faster. This can be done by either upgrading to the tier 3 upgrade and using Puddle Punch while in ball form, or timing Puddle Punch before activating Goo Ball.

**Air Vent Puddle Boosting**[1] can allow for large cross lane traversal. By chaining these boosts across multiple air vents, you can travel large swaths of distance, or even the entire map.

## The Cube

[edit | edit source]

*The Cube* is Viscous’ second ability. Upon casting, you encase either you or a teammate in a healing goo cube. *The Cube* can be cancelled at any time by the person who is cubed. *The Cube* acts as a normal physics object; it can fall, maintain momentum and be moved like a normal prop. Teammates and opponents are able to move the cubed by using Heavy Melee on them. Viscous is able to move *The Cube* using *Puddle Punch*.

*The Cube* has a lower friction coefficient while on the ground, being *0.8* instead of *4.0*.

| Slope Acceleration |  |
| --- | --- |
| Slope Acceleration |  |
| Tech Type: | Character Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Inputs: | *The Cube* |

### Slope Acceleration

[edit | edit source]

While in *The Cube*, the normal of the last touched surface is stored; this is speculated to be for velocity calculations while on slopes and ramps. During normal use while on the ground, *The Cube* acts normally and slides down slopes and ramps. This stored normal is not cleared while in the air; this means that if the last touched ground surface was a ramp, that normal will be stored, and the game will assume that you are currently on a slope and thus give you velocity in the direction of the slope. This phenomenon is called **Slope Acceleration**.

The stored normal will not update through abilities, Ziplines, jumps and air dashes. Upon touching the ground, the normal will be updated and acceleration reset.

To execute, be airborne and have your last grounded surface be a slope or a ramp. While airborne, use *The Cube*. You should observe *The Cube* being pushed whilst in the air towards the normal of the surface.

The velocity is constantly stacked on while in the air; while using Slope Acceleration and given enough time, you will accelerate to extremely high velocities (maximum ~*2000* u/s).

Slope Acceleration also works in *Goo Ball* form. When exiting *The Cube* while in *Goo Ball*, your downwards velocity will be paused for a brief second.

Slope Acceleration can be useful in conjunction with pre-defined rollouts; Slope Acceleration can allow for extremely fast traversal and rotations to predefined locations on the map. However, the usage of *The Cube* (an extremely powerful support ability) can limit the usefulness of this technique.

## Goo Ball

[edit | edit source]

*Goo Ball* is Viscous’ fourth and ultimate ability. Upon activation, you inflate into a large ball and move forwards at a constant velocity[2]. *Goo Ball* has a radius of *1.4* m, or *55* units[3] and an hurtbox of *1.8* m, or *70.9* units[4]. The radius increases with *+Ability Range*.

Upon activation, you will start accelerating to *445±1* u/s over the course of a second. While in *Goo Ball* form, you have limited turning controls and are forced to always move forwards. You are able to accelerate to *792.50* u/s over the course of three seconds by holding (by default) M1, sacrificing turning control for speed. Upon hitting a wall, you pause for a split second then rebound off; if you were accelerating beforehand, you will have to accelerate back up to peak speeds from your base speed.

While in ball form, you are able to Jump. You are also able to Air Jump without using Stamina.

Upon upgrading *Goo Ball* to its third AP upgrade, you unlock the use of other abilities and items in ball form. This allows for more complex movement techniques.

### Cube Turnaround

[edit | edit source]

Upon upgrading *Goo Ball* to its third AP upgrade, you unlock the use of other abilities and items in ball form.

By using *The Cube* while in *Goo Ball*, then cancelling, your previous momentum will be reversed (e.g. if you are moving forwards, then use *The Cube*, afterwards you will move backwards).

This can be useful for chain-stunning opponents or for routing.

### Frogpunch

[edit | edit source]

* Majestic Leap* is a Vitality item. The active ability of this item allows you to leap into the air, then quickly descend.

By rolling in *Goo Ball*, casting *Puddle Punch* onto a wall, bouncing off the wall then quickly using  *Majestic Leap*, you can leap much further into the air than normal. This is called a **Frogpunch**. To execute this, you need to upgrade *Goo Ball* to its third upgrade, which allows you to use other abilities and items while in ball form.

To execute, cast *Goo Ball*, and start accelerating. Be near a wall and cast *Puddle Punch* on it in preparation. Bounce off the wall, use  *Majestic Leap*, then get punched by *Puddle Punch*. The timing for the Frogpunch is tight. You have to bounce off the wall, cast  *Majestic Leap*[5] and then get hit by Puddle Punch, in that order.

This can be useful for traversing large distances or rotating; you can travel nearly half of the map using a single Frogpunch.

### Ball-less Frogpunch

[edit | edit source]

Frogpunch is able to be executed without *Goo Ball*. However, the **Ball-less Frogpunch** does not go as far as a normal Frogpunch.

The execution of the Ball-less Frogpunch is nearly the same as a normal Frogpunch, but without *Goo Ball.*

To execute, be hit by *Puddle Punch* and then use  *Majestic Leap*. If done correctly, you will go further than a regular  *Majestic Leap* or a regular Puddle Punch Boost.

### Magic Carpet Goo Ball

[edit | edit source]

* Magic Carpet* is a Spirit item that allows the user to cast a magic carpet for 8 seconds, allowing you to fly around the map.

Upon upgrading *Goo Ball* to its third AP upgrade, you unlock the use of other abilities and items in ball form. By casting  *Magic Carpet* while in the ball, you are able to be in *Goo Ball* and ride the carpet at the same time.

Riding the  *Magic Carpet* while in *Goo Ball* form does have some advantages:

- You still maintain the hitbox of the Goo Ball; this allows you to still do damage while flying around.
- You have full flying controls; you are able to make incredibly sharp turns while still damaging opponents.

When you hit an enemy opponent or minion while in carpet state,  *Magic Carpet* will disappear.

To execute, cast *Goo Ball*. After ballooning to ball size, use  *Magic Carpet*. After the cast time of  *Magic Carpet*, you should still be in ball form but be riding the carpet.

| March 6, 2026 | - Splatter bounces once by default. - Splatter cooldown reduced from 30s to 26. - Splatter spirit scaling reduced from 1.77 to 0.8. - Splatter ground effect now increases slide distance by 60% for you and your allies. - Splatter multiple hit damage value reduced from 50% to 50/38/26%. - Splatter T1 radius increased from +1m to +2m. - Splatter T2 cooldown increased from -12s to -14s. - Splatter T3 spirit scaling increased from +0.4 to +1.3. - Splatter T3 still adds 2 bounces. - The Cube now has a very brief period where allies cannot cancel to prevent accidental cancels. - The Cube healing spirit scaling increased from 0.14 to 0.3. - The Cube T3 increased from -21s Cooldown to -25s. - Puddle Punch now grants +30% Air Control when affecting yourself or allies. - Puddle Punch Charge Time increased from 1.5s to 1.7s. - Puddle Punch Slow increased from 15% to 20%. - Puddle Punch now acts as if its close range with respect to item procs (like  Point Blank) - Puddle Punch radius reduced from 4.5m to 4m. - Puddle Punch T2 changed from "+27 Damage and -15% Move Slow" to "+1.5m Radius and +30 Damage". - Goo Ball no longer can carry Urn. - Goo Ball turn rate improved a bit. - Goo Ball can now use abilities and items (rather than being locked behind T3) - Goo Ball cooldown increased from 115s to 130s. - Goo Ball duration increased from 9s to 10s. - Goo Ball Bullet and Spirit resist reduced from 60% to 35%. - Goo Ball T1 changed from "+5s Duration" to "-30s Cooldown". - Goo Ball T2 reduced from +72 Damage to +70. - Goo Ball T3 changed from "Can now use abilities and items" to "+6s duration and +0.3s Stun Duration". |
| January 30, 2026 | - Spirit per boon increased from 1.1 to 1.3. - Bullet damage per boon reduced from +0.5 to +0.36. - The Cube T3 no longer removes ult debuffs. - Puddle Punch displacement duration reduced from 1s to 0.8s. |
| November 21, 2025 | - Splatter cooldown increased from 21s to 30s. - Splatter T1 changed from "-6s Cooldown" to "+40 Damage and +1m Radius". - Splatter T2 changed from "+45 Damage and +1m Radius" to "-12s Cooldown". - Splatter T3 now also increases spirit scaling by 0.4. - The Cube duration reduced from 4s to 3s. - The Cube regen increased from 30 to 40. - The Cube T2 now also increases duration by +1s. |
| October 2, 2025 | - Alt fire base damage reduced from 48 to 42 - Alt fire damage growth increased from 1.25 to 1.6 - Splatter damage reduced from 80 to 70 - Splatter T1 increased from -5.75s to -6s |

Damage is now 100%, 50%, 50% for first, second and third hit. - Goo Ball damage reduced from 140 to 120. - **(Undocumented)**  Goo Ball no longer stuns Walkers. |

| December 6, 2024 | - Fixed visual parry cooldown bug with  Puddle Punch. - The Cube cooldown reduced from 48s to 42s. - The Cube cast range reduced from 30m to 26m. - Puddle Punch radius increased from 4 to 4.5. - Puddle Punch slow reduced from 20% to 15%. - Puddle Punch T2 slow reduced from 20% to 15%. - Puddle Punch T3 now also causes the Punch to become a heavy melee. - Goo Ball damage Spirit Power scaling reduced from 1.3 to 1.1. - Goo Ball damage T2 reduced from 120 to 90. |

| October 24, 2024 | - Viscous: cleaner effect for viscous alt-fire. - Bullet damage reduced from 12 to 11. - Bullet damage growth per boon increased from 0.86 to 0.9 (total from 24.04 to 23.6). - The Cube T2 moved to T3. - The Cube T2 is now +35 HP regen. - Splatter T2 reduced from +60 Damage to +50. - Goo Ball Spirit Resist reduced from 70% to 60%. |

| September 12, 2024 | - Viscous  Splatter effects have been adjusted. - Puddle Punch now correctly knocks people in  The Cube up in the air. - Improved various issues with the camera. - Puddle punch now telegraphs an effect before it forms. - Base bullet damage reduced from 14 to 13. - Splatter damage reduced from 110 to 100. - Goo Ball turn rate improved a bit. - Goo Ball stun frequency cooldown improved from 1.5s to 1.25s. - Fixed  Puddle Punch piercing  Unstoppable. |

**Vortex Web** is a Tier 4  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**. Its component,  Slowing Hex, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

- Vortex Web can be cast at a target enemy player, pulling other enemies towards them.
- The Vortex Web model is an octopus that pulls players with its arms.

“

Gotta be slippery in this business.

**Vyper** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. After Slithering across the battlefield to swiftly avoid enemy attacks while spraying them with copious amount of bullets, Vyper can inject retreating foes with Lethal Venom to finish them off and use her Screwjab Dagger to hit faraway targets. By slinging her Petrifying Bolas, Vyper will make sure that her targets won't get away from her.

Vyper is an impulsive outlaw that gets thrown in jail as many times as she escapes it, building a reputation among a number of criminal allies and enemies across the New Jersey Tri-State Area.

Vyper was added to Hero Labs as "Viper" on October 24, 2024, and officially released on January 17, 2025.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Vyper/Lore** for more story content.*

“

When it comes to breaking the law, not getting caught is a pretty important part of the job.  Vyper never got that memo.  Luckily for her, if there’s one thing she’s better at than being arrested, it’s escaping out of jail.

Having done time in every major prison in the tri-state area, Vyper has built an impressive network of street level lowlifes that owe her one.  She’s also built an impressive network of street level lowlifes that want her dead, but she tries to focus on the positive.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Vyper's current appearance is a modified version of *Neon Prime's*  Kali. Vyper's files also replaced some of Kali's original files.
- Vyper's lead developer is Hopoo,[3] best known as the co-creator of the *Risk of Rain* series.
- Before the 2025-10-02 Update, Vyper was the only hero who started with an unlocked ability by default (Slither).
- According to her voice actress Stephanie Kerbis, Vyper is "not from Wisconsin or New Jersey".[1]
- "Making Pruno in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Vyper in the Hideout.

You ever get the feeling that something bad is gonna happen?... Yeah so, I don't, that's why I end up in jail so much.

When it comes to breaking the law, not getting caught is a pretty important part of the job.  Vyper never got that memo.  Luckily for her, if there’s one thing she’s better at than being arrested, it’s escaping out of jail.

Having done time in every major prison in the tri-state area, Vyper has built an impressive network of street level lowlifes that owe her one.  She’s also built an impressive network of street level lowlifes that want her dead, but she tries to focus on the positive.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Vyper's wish seems to be a new and secure life for herself.[1][2][3]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Vyper is a gorgon.[4][5] She often refers to herself as "V".[6][7]

Vyper has been to New Jersey,[8] Staten Island,[9] Philadelphia,[10] Illinois,[11] Oklahoma[12] and Wisconsin.[13] She has been incarcerated (and escaped from) Riker's Island multiple times.[14] She doesn't want to be sent to Lost Whisper.[15]

Vyper used to work for the Mendoza Syndicate, acting as Infernus' replacement.[16][17] When working for Mendoza, Vyper was caught by Ivy and tried for 13 counts of murder, although Vyper mentions that the actual kill count was way higher.[18][19] Vyper has killed tourists in the past and felt no remorse for doing so.[20]

Vyper says her mother was "slinging poison" after she found out about a life insurance policy, implying that she murdered her spouse for the insurance.[21] Similarly, Vyper wants to get married to a rich husband and kill him for the inheritance.[22]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Vyper calls herself a "degenerate"[23] and has "real bad impulse control".[24]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Vyper has been kicked out of the Paradox Museum and the Baroness Hotel.[25][26] She's also been barred from Jezebel's.[27] Vyper once crashed Fashion Week.[28]

Vyper makes references to pruno, an improvised alcoholic beverage also known as "prison wine".[29][30]

Vyper has a Midwest accent, according to Mina.[31] Though according to Vyper's voice actress Stephanie Kerbis, Vyper is "not from Wisconsin or New Jersey".[32]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Billy

[edit | edit source]

Billy and Vyper are familiar with each other. While on the same team, Billy and Vyper flirt with each other. Vyper asks if she can call Billy "Lash", to which Billy doesn't care.[33]

While Vyper holds Billy in high regard,[34][35] Billy thinks Vyper is a moron.[36][37]

It's implied that Vyper knew Billy from before he got his goat head.[38]

### Lash

[edit | edit source]

Vyper is infatuated with Lash.[39][40][41] She has watched him sleep (without his knowledge)[42] and sends Lash letters made to "stand out" (the contents of the letters are unknown, but they do make Lash uncomfortable).[43][44] When Vyper flirts with  Billy, she asks if she can call him "Lash".[33]

Lash is scared of Vyper's obession with him and wants her to leave him alone.[45][46][47]

### Silver

[edit | edit source]

Silver has hunted and caught Vyper so many times that Vyper's use of  Petrifying Bola comes from Silver's  Entangling Bola.[14][48]

### Wraith

[edit | edit source]

Wraith wants Vyper dead since she once robbed one of Wraith's poker rooms.[49][50] She also doesn't allow Vyper to take out markers (informal loans) since Vyper never pays them back.[51][52] Vyper knows Sophia Arroyo works for Wraith.[53]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Nobody trusts Vyper,[54] with the exception of Rem.[55][56]
- Vyper dislikes  Bebop, Lash's pitfighting rival.[57]
- Aside from Lash, Vyper is attracted to Abrams,[58][59] Billy[33] and Mirage.[60] She also likes Cinnamon, a "librarian" from "Pole Palace" who resembles Paige.[61]
- Vyper likes  Mo & Krill.[62] They don't like her.[63]
- Vyper believes  Infernus "used to be hard, but now he's just a bitch".[64] She also liked Shiv before he went straight.[65][66]
- Vyper says her Screwjab Daggers are better than  Shiv's Serrated Knives.[67]
- Vyper says  Calico has a reputation of "sloppy work" due to "a hit that went bad" (a possible reference to the attempted assassination of  Pocket).[68]
- Vyper nicknames Paige "Red" and knew her brother, Bryce.[69][70]
- Vyper comments on  Grey Talon's health, due to his age.[71]
- Vyper wants  Mirage to "stop yelling about the Djinn".[72]
- Vyper is interested in stealing Ava,[73] Graves' lich hand,[74] Kelvin's parka,[75] Lady Geist's earrings,[76] Pocket's suitcase[77] and Yamato's sword.[78] She's robbed the Shopkeeper before.[79]
- Haze mentions that eliminating cretins like Vyper is beneath her pay grade.[80]
- Ivy is familar with Vyper from when she worked for Mendoza.[81][18][19]

# Walker

| Walker |  |

**Walkers** are one of the two types of defenses protecting the Patron, along with Guardians. They are very large metal automatons with four legs that hold a strange disc in their hands, which they use as a weapon.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Fire Beam
- 1.2 Stomp
- 1.3 Fireballs
- 2 Resistances

- 2.1 Backdoor protection
- 3 Destruction

- 3.1 Extra Slots
- 4 Update history
- 5 Gallery
- 6 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Walkers are the second line of defense in each lane, and can only be damaged after their corresponding Guardian has been destroyed. In total, there are **3** Walkers on each team with one individual in each lane. Walkers start with 6000 HP. As each Walker dies, the remaining Walkers have increased HP, with 9000 for two remaining Walkers and 12000 for one remaining Walker (the Walkers get a flat 3000 HP increase and heal when the other Walkers die). They also increase in size.

Walkers provide nearby allied heroes (28m) 15% Bullet and 15% Spirit Resistance. Walkers currently do not take headshot damage anywhere on their bodies.

The Walker is surrounded by two white circles on the ground. The smaller circle indicates the Walker's stomp range, and the larger circle indicates the Walker's range to take damage and to use their fireballs.

Like Guardians, Walkers are immune to all damage when no enemies are within 22m. When an enemy enters this range, the Walker becomes vulnerable, prioritizing the closest target to it.

When attacking, a Walker has three attacks it can use. All the attacks deal Spirit Damage and can be mitigated by Spirit Resist.

#### Fire Beam

[edit | edit source]

Channels a constantly damaging beam onto the nearest target. Deals 2% Max HP per second as Spirit Damage.

#### Stomp

[edit | edit source]

The Walker stomps the ground, dealing Spirit Damage and stunning enemies for 2 seconds in a 15m radius. Deals 350 damage as well as 15% Max HP as damage. A Walker will only ever use this attack if an enemy gets within 15m of it. The Walker cannot use Fire Beam or Fireballs when stomping.

#### Fireballs

[edit | edit source]

The Walker's Rocket Barrage (also known as Fireball Spray) launches a volley of 6 projectiles. Each projectile deals 200 Spirit Damage on impact and leaves a patch of fire on the ground. The fire lasts for 5 seconds and deals 25 damage per second to enemies standing in it. Additionally, the fireballs apply a debuff that reduces Bullet and Spirit resistance by 10%. This ability has a cooldown of 10 seconds.

## Resistances

[edit | edit source]

Walkers possess a high resistance to damage early in the game that degrades over time. They start with 65% Damage Resistance, which decays linearly down to -65% Resistance (taking increased damage) over the first 18 minutes of the match. Additionally, they possess 25% Bullet Resistance, but have no Spirit Resistance.

Walkers also take less weapon damage for each additional enemy within 51m, from 20% (3 enemies) to 50% (6 enemies). If there's only one or two enemies nearby, it has no additional resistance.

### Backdoor protection

[edit | edit source]

Like Shrines and Base Guardians, the Walker has a Backdoor Protection represented by a green circular effect around them, if the player attacks the Walker while their lane hasn't been pushed up to its position. When backdoor protection is active, the Walker gains 65% damage reduction from players and regenerates 65 health per second.

Since the lane progress depends on the position of the last trooper wave, the Walker still has backdoor protection until the active enemy trooper wave reaches the Walker's position.

## Destruction

[edit | edit source]

When a team destroys a Walker, it awards a total of  **4000**. The bounty is divided among attackers in two parts: First, 40% ( **1,600**) is split between all nearby attacking players (including those that did damage to the walker in the last 20 seconds). The remaining 60% ( **2,400**) is then distributed equally among all six members of the attacking team, regardless of their location.

#### Extra Slots

[edit | edit source]

Each Walker destroyed unlocks one Extra Slot for the entire team.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The current Walker model is called the **Sun Walker** in the files.
- The Walker used to have a model called the **Wax Walker**. It was functionally similar to the Sun Walker, with 4 legs and 2 arms, but the legs were made of candle wax and the arms were attached to the underside of the body, which was shaped like an iron cauldron. The Wax Walker was used during the beginning of the current playtest, from April to May 2024, when it was replaced by the Sun Walker.
- A new work-in-progress Walker model labeled **Clock Tower** was added to the game files in the Six New Heroes update.
- In *Neon Prime*, the Walkers were carried by a dropship and dropped in the lanes at the start of the game.

# Walking

“Cannot waste time.”

Overview

Sprinting

| Walking |  |
| --- | --- |

Walking is the most common movement action in **Deadlock**. Walking allows your character to navigate around the Cursed Apple.

When you start walking, you will begin to start accelerating towards a peak speed which is dependent on character, which can be increased with items.[1] When you stop walking, you will gradually decelerate to a complete stop.[2]

You can also walk while crouching. When crouch walking, you will move at a speed of **4.75 m/s**.

##### Characters Whose Move Speed Increases with Spirit Power

[edit | edit source]

Certain characters have move speed that scales with Spirit Power (indicated by the *x* symbol). Move speed increases by a fixed coefficient that varies by character.

For example,  Grey Talon’s move speed scales with Spirit Power at a coefficient of *x*0.0084. If Grey Talon purchases  Boundless Spirit and reaches a total of 82 Spirit Power, he gains an additional **0.66 m/s** of move speed.

| Character | Base Move Speed (m/s) | *x* Scaling Coefficient |

| Sinclair | 7.2 | *x*0.0138 |
| Vyper | 6.9 | *x*0.0138 |

[edit | edit source]

# Walking/Sprinting

Overview

Sprinting

| Sprinting |  |
| --- | --- |
| Sprinting |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Move (WASD) |

All characters have the ability to Sprint. Sprinting in **Deadlock** is a passive action — no further action is required to sprint. When sprinting, you instantly accelerate up to +2.5 m/s of your base sprint speed[1]), then gain 0.6 m/s every second[2]) above that threshold. Sprinting characters can be identified by the grey speed lines coming off them. You cannot sprint while zooming in using alt-fire).

Every character has a base sprint speed of 1.6 m/s except:

- Bebop – 4 m/s
- Kelvin – 1.1 m/s
- Lady Geist – 2.4 m/s
- Lash – 2.1 m/s
- Paige – 3.5 m/s
- Victor – 1.1 m/s

When characters are sprinting:

- If they have been damaged by an enemy hero, sprint will be disabled for 3 seconds, which can be significantly slower.
- If they have been damaged by a non-hero, sprint will be disabled for 3 seconds).[3]
- If they are firing, they will move significantly slower (around ~70% of their base walk speed) until the character stops firing.

- With the  Weapon Item  Fleetfoot, they will move at their base walk speed if they are firing.
- Ivy’s  Kudzu Connection, provides Fleetfoot's passive to both her and the tethered teammate.

# Wall Jumping

Overview

Corner Boost

Edge Boost

Fast Climb

| Wall Jumping |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load video     Local File     Local File might collect personal data.     Continue Dismiss  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Walljumping.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Stamina: | 0Initially, 0.5After the first wall jump in the air |
| Inputs: | Be near a wall then jump. Can be angled using movement keys. |

**Wall Jumping** is an additional action available to you in the air which allows you to jump off the wall. Wall Jumping does not count towards the Air Jump limit.

Every subsequent Wall Jump after the first where you don't touch the ground costs *0.5* stamina.

Wall Jumping is only available whilst airborne. While in the air, if you jump while near a wall, you will execute a Wall Jump. If successful, you should see a brown/beige dust circle around the initial jumping point.

While in the air, you technically have infinite wall jumps. However, subsequent wall jumps after the first can be fatigued (have a weaker vertical launch) if timed incorrectly and will cost *0.5* stamina.

Wall Jumping allows you to scale walls more efficiently, acting essentially as a third jump or as a complete replacement for air jumping. It is useful in the laning phase, where you do not have as much stamina to spend, since the first one does not consume any stamina.

Wall Jumps are able to be angled up or downwards depending on the movement key used relative to the wall.

- If the movement key pressed is towards the wall, you will have an upwards angled Wall Jump, with high vertical velocity but low horizontal velocity. This type of Wall Jump has no variation in angle; every upwards angled Wall Jump is the same.
- If the movement key pressed is away from the wall, you will have a outwards angled Wall Jump, with high horizontal velocity but low vertical velocity.

- If you are using a controller or have an analog joystick, outwards angled Wall Jumps can have slight variations depending on joystick angle.

Wall Jumps apply a significant amount of air drag onto your character. However, this air drag is the same air drag that is removed when hopping off ziplines, which allows you to bypass the air drag using **Zipline Momentum Conservation**.

### Wall Jump Fatigue

[edit | edit source]

You are able to execute multiple Wall Jumps in succession; the first Wall Jump is normal, but subsequent wall jumps have significantly weaker vertical launch. This mechanic is called **Wall Jump Fatigue**.

Wall Jump Fatigue is an invisible meter which determines the power of your next Wall Jump. When you Wall Jump, you are fatigued for *1.25* seconds. Attempting to Wall Jump in this time period will result in a *weakened Wall Jump*, and the fatigue meter will be set back to *1.25* seconds. Upon landing, Wall Jump Fatigue is reset to normal levels.

While in the air, both types of melee (Light Melee and Heavy Melee) will trigger Wall Jump Fatigue.

# Wall Jumping/Corner Boosting

Overview

Corner Boost

Edge Boost

Fast Climb

| Corner Boosting |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load video     Local File     Local File might collect personal data.     Continue Dismiss  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Cornerboost.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Wall Jump on an edge, corner or curved surface |

**Corner Boosting** is an exploit that is the result of a buggy interaction between Wall Jumps and map geometry, allowing players to gain significantly more height than a standard wall jump. This technique can be performed on any edge, corner or curved surface but requires precise positioning and timing.

When you attempt to Wall Jump, the game will check the closest point on the wall from your collision capsule to determine your launch angle and vector. When near the edge of a horizontal and vertical surface or on a curved surface, the resulting angle, and therefore vector, can become incredibly steep, and (after addition with other vectors) result in an incredibly steep resulting vector. This is further helped with the shape of the collision capsule and its rounded shape, allowing for even higher angles. This results in a Wall Jump with near to no horizontal velocity (depending on the surface) and high vertical velocity.

## Contents

- 1 Visual Comparison
- 2 Methods to execute a Corner Boost

- 2.1 Regular Method
- 2.2 Dropdown Method
- 2.3 Light Melee Mantle Method
- 2.4 Dash Jump Method
- 2.5 Downdash Method

#### Visual Comparison

[edit | edit source]

| Fig. 1 Fig. 2 | | Key |  | | --- | --- | | ■ Light Blue | Collision capsule | | ■ Red | Absolute velocity | | ■ Green | Sideways velocity | | ■ Orange | Wall push | | ■ Purple | Final velocity | |
| --- | --- |
| This is an illustrative diagram showing the game calculations behind Corner Boosting.  - Fig. 1 shows a normal Wall Jump. Since the surface is a normal vertical wall, the push vector is angled 90°. Combined with the other set vectors (a set sideways vector and a set upwards vector, which normally make you ascend in a normal Wall Jump), this creates a slightly upward angled final vector, in which you travel. - Fig. 2 shows a Corner Boost. Since the surface being Wall Jumped off is angled upwards, the resulting angle and therefore vector is angled accordingly. This vector is added to other set vectors to create a steep final vector, in which you travel. |  |

Corner Boosting has several practical uses:

- It grants more height than a normal wall jump, which can be very useful for traversal around the map. Corner Boosts can be used to scale buildings or escape enemy pressure on the ground.
- Corner Boosting can provide an advantage in combat. This is especially useful for  Lash, whose  Ground Strike gains damage depending on the height when used.
- The height gained from a Corner Boost can allow you to peek over obstacles (e.g., bridges, barrels) for better sightlines.
- Certain characters who have abilities that require sightlines to properly work benefit greatly (e.g.,  Vindicta's  Assassinate,  Bebop's  Grapple Arm)

Corner Boosting works on all surfaces to varying extents; edges of a horizontal and vertical plane are best and provide the most vertical distance, but curved surfaces (e.g. Midboss Roof, Golden Idol statues, Hotdog Stand) can provide a near optimal Corner Boost as well.

#### Methods to execute a Corner Boost

[edit | edit source]

There are various methods and setups to execute a Corner Boost, varying in difficulty, consistency and applicability. All methods give the same result; whatever method you choose is up to personal preference and the situation at hand.

##### Regular Method

 Regular Corner Boost

The **Regular Method** is the least complicated method to Corner Boost off objects.

To execute a Regular Method Corner Boost, simply jump towards an object (e.g. stone fencing) and Wall Jump off the side. This can be harder than other methods due to the variability in jump velocity and initial standing position.

##### Dropdown Method

[edit | edit source]

 

Load video

 

Local File

 

Local File might collect personal data.

 

Continue Dismiss

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Dropdowncornerboost.mp4

 Dropdown Corner Boost

The **Dropdown Method** is a method to Corner Boost off objects with a thin ledge by mantling. The object being Corner Boosted off are usually signposts of varying sizes.

To execute a Dropdown Method Corner Boost:

- Mantle onto the signpost then drop down. Depending on the width of the object you might not have to input additional movement keys to drop down.
- When you are near the edge of the object, press the jump key to Corner Boost. If you are struggling to get the input down, look down towards the edge to better gauge when to press jump.

This method is especially useful in lane; Corner Boosting off signposts near building rooftops can allow for surprise attacks on opponents farming or characters that like to camp on the rooftop early on (such as  Vindicta or  Grey Talon).

##### Light Melee Mantle Method

[edit | edit source]

 

Load video

 

Local File

 

Local File might collect personal data.

 

Continue Dismiss

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Lmmcornerboost.mp4

 Light Melee Mantle Corner Boost

By running towards a short mantleable ledge, using Light Melee then mantling, you can setup a consistent Corner Boost using the **Light Melee Mantle Method**Also known as Melee Mantle. This method is near exclusively done on small stone fencing found near the river of the map. This method abuses a property where Light Melee reduces momentum, allowing a player to be closer to the fencing.

To execute this method:

- Sprint towards the object you want to mantle on.
- When you are in mantle range, Light Melee and hold the jump key to buffer a mantle.
- If done correctly, your character will appear to be using a Light Melee while floating up the ledge.
- After this, press jump to Corner Boost.

This method is useful because it is extremely consistent, reliable and applicable. The method nearly always allows for a Corner Boost and the stone fencing usually Corner Boosted off is found throughout the map in various locations.

##### Dash Jump Method

[edit | edit source]

 

Load video

 

Local File

 

Local File might collect personal data.

 

Continue Dismiss

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Dashjumpcornerboost.mp4

 Dash Jump Corner Boost

The **Dash Jump Method** is one of the harder methods to execute a Corner Boost. It consists of precisely Dash Jumping towards an object and Corner Boosting off the edge/corner. Objects that are Corner Boosted off using this method are usually much taller than other objects (one example is the large brick walls in the Sandbox in lane). This method requires the player to have a good gauge on the distance of a Dash Jump.

To execute:

- Dash Jump towards the object you want to Corner Boost off. The initial point at which you start the Dash Jump matters; try to be ~14—15 metres away from the object.
- When sufficiently near the objects edge/corner, jump to Corner Boost.

This method is useful in the jungle, where there are lots of objects that can be Dash Jump Corner Boosted off (e.g. the hotdog stand).

##### Downdash Method

[edit | edit source]

 

Load video

 

Local File

 

Local File might collect personal data.

 

Continue Dismiss

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Downdashcornerboost.mp4

 Downdash Corner Boost

The **Downdash method** is one of the hardest methods to execute a Corner Boost. In this method, you jump off the side of an edge then Downdash towards it to Corner Boost. This method relies heavily on precise timing and prior speed.

To execute Downdash Method:

- Run backwards towards an edge and jump. Make sure that when you jump, you are near the ledge.
- Once over the edge, Downdash. Make sure that you are very slightly over the ledge, so that you are in a position to jump off of it later.
- When sufficiently near the ledge, jump.

This method is near impractical due to its difficulty and variability. However, if you can execute it consistently, it is the fastest way to set up a Corner Boost, and will allow you to Corner Boost of nearly anything instantly.

# Wall Jumping/Edge Boost

Overview

Edge Boost

| Edge Boosting |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load video     Local File     Local File might collect personal data.     Continue Dismiss  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Edgeboost.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Wall Jump on a vertical edge while moving. |

**Edge Boosting** are a variation of Wall Jumps, allowing players to gain extra horizontal distance in their current velocity direction by Wall Jumping off the edge of a wall. While Edge Boosts share a similar name to Corner Boosts, they function differently.

When near a wall, the game will detect the closest point to your collision capsule and use the normal of it to determine which way you are going to Wall Jump. When Edge Boosting, you are attempting to shift the normal towards your intended momentum (typically forwards or backwards) by Wall Jumping as late as you can.

Edge Boosting is in essence a normal Wall Jump, unlike Corner Boosts; you do not trade off vertical impulse for horizontal impulse. Instead, you "stack" your Wall Jump velocity with already pre-existing velocity.

Edge Boosting is particularly great for preserving momentum, since you lose less forwards velocity compared to a regular Wall Jump. Edge Boosting is extremely hard to execute in a real game, since you cannot hang off an edge with your collision capsule the way you can with Corner Boosts and the window to Wall Jump with the best normal is typically one or two ticks. While difficult, Edge Boosting can be mastered for efficient rollouts and escape routes that are hard to follow.

To execute, Wall Jump off an edge as late as you can for the maximum velocity. Take advantage of Wall Sliding to time the input.

| Fast Climbing |  |

| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Fastclimb.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Stamina: | 0 |
| Inputs: | Hold the forward movement key and press jump twice. |

Fast Climbing is a way of quickly climbing vertical walls by Wall Jumping and holding the jump key to buffer a mantle. It can typically be done on walls that can be mantled with an air jump. The main benefit of Fast Climbing is that it allows you to climb walls that would’ve taken an air jump.

Fast Climbs do not consume any stamina.

Fast Climbing allows you to scale buildings easily without burning stamina. Without Fast Climbing, you could air jump and waste one stamina bar; or wall jump and Heavy Melee, which is slower and debuffs your subsequent Wall Jumps for two seconds..

To Fast Climb, look directly at the wall you want to climb. While moving into the wall, wall jump holding the forward movement key. If you are close to the edge, you will automatically mantle; if not, you can air jump, Heavy Melee or use another movement option to climb the wall.

“

First they panic, and then, they die.

**Warden** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He is a tough, tenacious brawler with a technique for alchemy and fighting the supernatural. Opening fights with either a Binding Word or a disrupting Alchemical Flask, Warden dashes into the fight to brawl at close range and utilizing his Willpower for protection and staying power. In desperate situations, Warden can trigger his Last Stand, damaging and stealing life from all foes in front of him.

The descendant of a long line of militant alchemists, Warden's ancestors once trained vigorously for the day they would have to stave off a mystic apocalypse. But as time passed, the meaning behind the training was lost, causing Warden's parents to be unprepared for the first maelstrom. With the apocalypse on the horizon, Warden was trained since birth, forged into a weapon built specifically towards stopping the Patrons from ever entering our world, no matter the cost.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Warden/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Most people think the supernatural came into the world 50 years ago.  They’re wrong.  Its presence shaped folklore for generations… and as long as there have been people afraid of the shadows, there have been those who dedicated their lives to fighting in them.

Coming from a lineage of militant alchemists, Warden’s family always trained for the day they would have to stave off a mystic apocalypse… but as time passed the importance of the lessons seemed less and less important.  What once was viewed as a sincere warning slowly morphed into being perceived as amusing anecdotes told by their superstitious grandparents.

When the portal opened in Central Park, Warden’s parents realized not only was everything they were told was true, they were unprepared.  Refusing to let the next generation fall asleep on the job, Warden was trained since birth to be a supernatural killing machine with one purpose: stopping the Patrons from ever entering our world.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Warden was named **Murphy** in *Neon Prime*. This name was reused for the new character of Captain Murphy in Holliday's visual novel.

- He may have been named after the protagonist of the 1987 movie *Robocop,* as Murphy was a robot peacekeeper in *Neon Prime's* sci-fi setting.
- Despite his appearance, Warden is not a police officer. A concept sketch for Warden's upcoming redesign can be seen in one of Yamato's concept artwork released by Yoshi.[1] The Shopkeeper may ask Warden if he would be interested in selling his cape, despite Warden's current model not having one.[2] The Newscaster voice line for Warden's Winter skin challenge also makes a reference to his upcoming redesign, asking "What will he look like next?"[3]
- Warden's backstory shares themes with Arc Warden from *Dota 2,* who similarly wants to stop the conflict between the Ancients at any cost.
- "Training in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Warden in the Hideout.
- Warden appears in a graffiti in the *Counter-Strike 2* community map "Warden".[4]

“

The Patrons must be stopped. No matter the cost.

Most people think the supernatural came into the world 50 years ago.  They’re wrong.  Its presence shaped folklore for generations… and as long as there have been people afraid of the shadows, there have been those who dedicated their lives to fighting in them.

Coming from a lineage of militant alchemists, Warden’s family always trained for the day they would have to stave off a mystic apocalypse… but as time passed the importance of the lessons seemed less and less important.  What once was viewed as a sincere warning slowly morphed into being perceived as amusing anecdotes told by their superstitious grandparents.

When the portal opened in Central Park, Warden’s parents realized not only was everything they were told was true, they were unprepared.  Refusing to let the next generation fall asleep on the job, Warden was trained since birth to be a supernatural killing machine with one purpose: stopping the Patrons from ever entering our world.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Warden's motivation in the ritual seems to be to stop the ritual and prevent the Patrons from being summoned.[1][2][3]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Before Warden was born, Warden's parents were living in New York, having neglected their duties in preparing for a mystic apocalypse. When the First Maelstrom occured, making the public aware of the existence of magic, Warden's parents realised that everything they had been told was true, and that the "mystic apocalypse" they had been warned about was now on the horizon. Having "failed to protect" New York,[4][5] Warden's parents made sure that their son, Warden, would not make the same mistake they did.[1] It's implied that Warden's militant alchemist bloodline comes from his father's side.[6]

Warden is said to be a vigilante,[7][8] although his feats are currently unknown. Warden mentions that New York is under his protection.[9]

Warden has no hobbies outside of his training.[10][11][12] Due to training his entire life,[13] Warden never got to live a normal childhood.[14] It's implied that he dreams of playing catch.[15]

How Warden intends to stop the Patrons is currently unknown, although Warden expresses that he "only gets one shot at this",[16] and is willing to die if it means completing his mission.[17]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

It's implied that Warden is miserable.[18][19]

Warden is implied to have trouble trusting people.[20] He seems to hide his motivations from his allies, based on his conversation with Holliday.[21]

Although Warden is committed to protecting humanity at all costs, he does not discriminate against supernatural creatures, instead treating characters like Abrams and Ivy with respect.[22][23]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Despite his appearance, Warden is not a police officer. A concept sketch for Warden's upcoming redesign can be seen in one of Yamato's concept artwork released by Yoshi.[24] The Shopkeeper may ask Warden if he would be interested in selling his cape, despite Warden's current model not having one.[25] The Newscaster voice line for Warden's Winter skin challenge also makes a reference to his upcoming redesign, asking "What will he look like next?"[26]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### The Patrons

[edit | edit source]

Warden hides his true motives from the Patrons, despite their telepathic abilities.[27][28] As such, the Patrons likely don't know that Warden is working against their goals. He is unable to hide his emotions from them, as the Patrons' heralds identify that Warden hates the Patrons and is afraid of failure.[29][30]

Warden views his battle with the Patrons as a war.[31][32]

### Grey Talon

[edit | edit source]

Warden once looked up to Grey Talon and heavily respects him.[33][34] When on opposing teams, Warden is shocked that Talon would willingly work for the Patrons.[35] While Grey Talon appreciates Warden's conviction,[36] he believes that both he and Warden live "hollow lives."[37]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Warden respects Ivy,[23] but he also believes she's "meddling in things she doesn't understand."[38]
- The Shopkeeper, Viscous and Vyper point out that Warden never smiles.[39][18][40]  Dynamo and  Lady Geist tell Warden that he looks "dour",[41] with Lady Geist also describing him as looking "perpetually miserable".[19]  Venator says that Warden fights as someone who wouldn't have chosen the life he has.[42]

- An unfinished conversation with  Grey Talon implies that, if Warden had a choice, he wouldn't have trained his whole life to fight the Patrons (Note that as Warden's own line is missing, it is uncertain if he accepts or denies it- Grey Talon merely expresses sorrow at his response).[43]
- Holliday thinks Warden has issues and calls him a "creepy homeschooled kid".[44][45] If they're on opposing teams, however, Holliday wishes that they were working together.[46]
- Like the Patrons, The Doorman is also unable to find out exactly what Warden wants, even when Warden is trapped in the Baroness Hotel.[47] He seems familiar with Warden's parents and derides them as failures.[6][48]
- Apollo respects Warden for his conviction and discipline.[49]
- Billy,[50]  Calico,[51]  Pocket[52] and  Mirage[53] call Warden out for his blind devotion to his parents' mission.

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

### Neon Prime - Murphy

[edit | edit source]

Warden was named **Murphy** in *Neon Prime*. This name was reused for the new character of Captain Murphy in Holliday's visual novel. He may have been named after the protagonist of the 1987 movie *Robocop,* as Murphy was a robot peacekeeper in *Neon Prime's* sci-fi setting.

# Warp Dash Jump

| Warp Dash Jump |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Warpdashing.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Item Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Hard |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Dash → Warp Stone → Jump (in dash jump window) |

Dashes open a window to Dash Jump. You do not have to be grounded or even still dashing after the initial press to dash jump.

The Jump part of a dash jump sets your velocity to a set amount (810 u/s). Normally, it is irrelevant, since it’s just the speed a regular grounded dash goes.

When dashing then using  Warp Stone, the window for dash jumping is still available. The resulting dash jump is a normal dash jump, and has the normal amount of speed, but happens after Warp Stone.

The direction that you dash in before warping is the direction of the dash jump; this allows you to create tricker movement.

This allows you to maintain speed after Warp Stone. Warp Dash Jump is particularly good for disengaging and escaping.

To execute, dash forward and use Warp Stone. After the warp, jump in the dash jump window. You should do a regular dash jump afterwards.

---

# Warp Dashing

| Warp Dashing |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Warpdashing.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Item Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Warp Stone → Air Dash |

When emerging from  Warp Stone, you are fully actionable and (typically) in the air. You can Air Dash after a Warp Stone to create tricky movement for your opponent.

Warp Dashing costs one bar of Stamina.

Warp Dashing can be used to confuse your opponent or turn corners. This can look to observers as if you have disappeared entirely.

Since Warp Stone kills all prior velocity, you can air dash the full distance without it fighting against prior velocity.

To execute, use Warp Stone and after you emerge, Air Dash in your chosen direction.

**Warp Stone** is a Tier 3  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Movement

[edit | edit source]

When activated, Warp Stone teleports you forward in the direction of the caster's camera, emitting a distinctive sound as you warp. Warp Stone only allows you to warp to positions that have a line of sight from where you start from; you are unable to warp through objects or walls. Alongside this, using Warp Stone immediately stops the caster's velocity on all axes.

When performing on the ground, you will be in the air for a very short amount of time; this allows you to execute actions that are available while in the air.

# Weapon Damage

**Weapon Damage** is a stat that determines the player's Bullet Damage, and also increases their Melee Damage. Some abilities can deal Weapon Damage.

## Base Weapon Properties

[edit | edit source]

### Base Bullet Damage

[edit | edit source]

Base Bullet Damage is the amount of damage your Hero deals with no items. This value is unique to each hero and increases automatically as you level up through Boons.

### Spreadshots

[edit | edit source]

Spreadshots allow certain weapons to fire multiple bullets at once (such as shotguns or shurikens). In these cases, all calculation rules apply to every individual bullet.

### Piercing shots

[edit | edit source]

Paige's weapon's shots pierce through enemies and can hit multiple enemies per projectile, disappearing only when they hit a map surface. However, they do not deal headshot bonus damage, but can proc headshot items.

The Doorman's weapon's shots also pierce enemies. Unlike Paige's, they can deal headshot damage but deal half damage to all enemies hit after the first.

### Melee Damage

[edit | edit source]

Melee Damage scales with Weapon Damage by 50%. However, Melee Damage is *not* considered Weapon Damage, thus effects that block Weapon Damage such as  Metal Skin have no effect against melee unless noted otherwise.

## Combat Modifiers

[edit | edit source]

### Damage Falloff

[edit | edit source]

Damage Falloff reduces damage based on distance. All heroes have a Falloff Range in which damage is linearly reduced from 100% to 10%.

When aiming at an enemy hero, a dot on their health bar indicates the percentage of damage you will deal:

| Dot Color | Damage Percentage |
| --- | --- |
| **Red** | 10% - 20% |
| **Orange** | 20% - 35% |
| **Yellow** | 35% - 75% |
| **Transparent** | 75% - 100% |

### Crit Multiplier

[edit | edit source]

Aiming for the head deals increased damage. Troopers, Guardians, and Heroes have a weakpoint hitbox that receives **1.65x** bullet damage when hit.

Crit Multiplier=[1+(0.65×Crit Bonus Scale)]×Crit Resist

The following heroes cannot deal critical damage:

- Graves
- Paige (though she can proc headshot item effects)

**Crit Bonus Scale** is a stat that modifies critical damage for certain heroes.

| Hero | Crit Bonus Scale (%) |
| --- | --- |
| Billy | -20 |
| Celeste | -25 |
| The Doorman | -25 |
| Drifter | -45 |
| Kelvin | -25 |
| Rem | -20 |
| Vyper | -30 |

Abilities that can deal critical damage have different critical modifiers. This replaces the +65% multiplier of base weapons.

| Hero | Ability | Crit Damage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paradox | Kinetic Carbine | 14 |
| Venator | Ira Domini | 30 |
| Vindicta | Assassinate | 20 |

## Target Modifiers

[edit | edit source]

### Bullet Resistance

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Damage Resistance

Incoming damage is reduced by the target's **Bullet Resist** and increased by the attacker's **Bullet Resist Reduction**. These stats stack multiplicatively. For a detailed breakdown on how multiple items stack, see the main page.

### Increased Bullet Damage

[edit | edit source]

Increased Bullet Damage is a debuff inflicted on enemies. It multiplies the total amount of damage they take from you. Because this is applied at the end of the calculation, it also increases the effectiveness of your Flat Weapon Damage.

## Flat Weapon Damage

[edit | edit source]

Flat Weapon Damage is an extra amount of damage obtained through certain hero abilities.

**Flat Weapon Damage is not increased by your "Weapon Damage %" multiplier.** It is an additive source added to your total *after* the percentage multiplier is applied to your base. However, it is still affected by Damage Falloff, Bullet Resist, and Crit Multipliers.

## Weapon Damage Formula

[edit | edit source]

The final damage dealt by a bullet is determined by multiplying your base stats, your item bonuses, and various situational modifiers.

Final Damage=[(Base Damage×Weapon Damage Multiplier)+Flat Bonus]×Falloff×Resistances×Crit Multiplier

## Weapon Damage Scaling

[edit | edit source]

Some abilities scale with Weapon Damage.

For most Weapon Damage scaling abilities, they only scale based on the "Bonus Weapon Damage" stat, which is granted by items and Weapon shop investments (see list below). This includes abilities such as  Venator's  Consecrating Grenade,  Gutshot and  Ira Domini.  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine is an exception, since it scales with her Base Weapon Damage (counting as a full burst shot), and thus increases with Boons. Melee Damage scaling abilities also scale with Weapon Damage, since Melee Damage scales with Weapon Damage (by 50%).
